hot_weather.description: Prefer lightweight, breathable garments and avoid unnecessary heavy layering.
examples: linen shirt + relaxed trousers + loafers
cotton t-shirt + lightweight trousers + sneakers

humid_weather.description: Choose breathable fabrics and comfortable silhouettes that allow airflow and reduce discomfort.
examples: relaxed cotton shirt + lightweight trousers + sneakers
breathable t-shirt + relaxed shorts + sneakers

cool_weather.description: Add appropriate layers while keeping the outfit's proportions and visual direction consistent.
examples: t-shirt + overshirt + jeans + sneakers
shirt + jacket + trousers + boots

wet_weather.description: Prefer practical fabrics, secure footwear and layers that can handle wet conditions.
examples: t-shirt + lightweight overshirt + dark trousers + sneakers
hoodie + cargo trousers + weather-resistant sneakers

rules.styling_tip: Prioritize real weather conditions first, then maintain colour, fit and style coordination.

rules.name: Outfit garment condition guidance
rules.guideline: The visible condition and neatness of garments can affect how polished and intentional the complete outfit appears.

polished_condition.description: Clean, well-maintained and appropriately pressed garments support polished styling.

casual_condition.description: Relaxed garments can have a naturally casual appearance, but they should still look clean and intentionally styled.

visible_issues.description: Obvious stains, excessive wrinkles, lint, stretched areas or damaged details can reduce the perceived neatness of an outfit.
examples: stained shirt
heavy lint on dark clothing
excessively wrinkled trousers
damaged footwear

rules.styling_tip: When analysing an outfit image, consider garment condition separately from colour, fit and style.

rules.name: Outfit skin exposure balance
rules.guideline: The amount and placement of visible skin can influence the overall balance and visual character of an outfit.

minimal_exposure.description: More covered outfits generally create a structured, polished or conservative appearance.

moderate_exposure.description: Controlled exposure such as short sleeves, an open collar or ankle visibility can keep casual outfits relaxed without becoming visually excessive.

higher_exposure.description: Shorts, sleeveless garments or more open layers create a more relaxed and expressive styling direction.

rules.styling_tip: Consider the total visible skin across the outfit rather than judging each exposed area separately.

rules.name: Outfit footwear visual connection
rules.guideline: Footwear should visually connect with at least one element of the outfit through colour, material, formality or overall style direction.

colour_connection.description: Footwear can repeat or complement a noticeable outfit colour.
examples: white sneakers with a white top
brown loafers with brown accessories

material_connection.description: Similar material or finish between footwear and another accessory can create visual continuity.
examples: brown leather loafers with a brown leather belt
suede sneakers with other matte-textured pieces

style_connection.description: Footwear should support the overall style direction instead of introducing an unrelated visual language.
examples: retro sneakers with relaxed streetwear
loafers with tailored smart-casual outfits
minimal sneakers with clean minimal outfits

rules.styling_tip: Check whether the footwear feels visually connected to the outfit rather than evaluating it as an isolated item.

rules.name: Sock visibility and coordination
rules.guideline: Sock visibility should support the footwear, trouser length and overall outfit style rather than appearing accidental.

no_show_socks.description: Low or hidden socks work well when a clean ankle-showing appearance is intended.

visible_neutral_socks.description: Neutral visible socks create a clean transition between trousers and footwear.

statement_socks.description: Noticeable socks can become a deliberate accent when their colour or pattern supports the outfit.

rules.styling_tip: When socks are visible, check their colour, pattern and visibility as part of the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit branding balance
rules.guideline: Visible logos and branding should support the outfit rather than creating unnecessary visual competition.

minimal_branding.description: Small or subtle logos work well when a clean and understated appearance is intended.

single_statement_logo.description: One noticeable logo can act as a deliberate visual detail while the remaining garments stay relatively simple.

multiple_logos.description: Several prominent logos can increase visual complexity, so the remaining outfit should generally stay controlled.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing an outfit image, identify whether visible branding is subtle, supportive or visually dominant.

rules.name: Outfit graphic density guidance
rules.guideline: The number and visual strength of graphics across garments can affect how busy or controlled an outfit appears.

single_graphic_focus.description: One prominent graphic garment can become the main visual element while the remaining pieces stay relatively simple.

low_graphic_density.description: Using mostly plain garments creates a cleaner visual field and allows silhouette, colour or accessories to stand out.

high_graphic_density.description: Multiple strong graphics increase visual complexity and should be used intentionally when a bold styling direction is desired.

rules.styling_tip: Evaluate the combined visual strength of garment graphics rather than judging each graphic individually.

rules.name: Outfit care consistency guidance
rules.guideline: Different garments may require different care levels, and visibly mismatched care can affect the overall presentation of an outfit.

clean_and_well_maintained.description: Garments and footwear should appear clean and maintained when the intended outfit is polished.

relaxed_care_appearance.description: Casual outfits can tolerate a more relaxed appearance, but visible dirt, heavy wear or neglected footwear can still distract from the styling.

mixed_condition.description: A highly polished garment combined with visibly worn or poorly maintained footwear can create an inconsistent overall presentation.
examples: formal trousers with heavily dirty sneakers
pressed shirt with visibly damaged footwear

rules.styling_tip: Assess the maintenance level of garments and footwear together when judging the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit layer removal coherence
rules.guideline: When an outer layer is removed, the remaining outfit should still look intentional and complete.

complete_without_outer_layer.description: The base outfit should work independently instead of depending entirely on the jacket, overshirt or outer layer.
examples: t-shirt + trousers + sneakers under an overshirt
shirt + trousers + loafers under a lightweight jacket

outer_layer_dependency.description: If the base layer is overly plain, visually incomplete or poorly coordinated, removing the outer layer can weaken the overall outfit.
examples: unfinished-looking base outfit revealed after removing jacket
outer layer hiding an otherwise disconnected combination

intentional_transition.description: Layered outfits should allow practical transitions between covered and uncovered states without losing their styling direction.

rules.styling_tip: Evaluate the outfit both with and without its outermost layer when analysing layered looks.

rules.name: Outfit dress-code signal guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit communicates a level of dress through garment choices, footwear and styling details, so the visual signal should match the expected dress code.

casual_signal.description: T-shirts, jeans, relaxed trousers and sneakers generally communicate a casual dress level.

smart_casual_signal.description: Collared shirts, polos, chinos, tailored trousers and clean loafers or minimal sneakers can communicate a refined but relaxed dress level.

formal_signal.description: Structured tailoring, dress shirts, formal trousers and appropriate dress footwear communicate a more formal dress level.

rules.styling_tip: Judge the combined dress-code signal of the complete outfit rather than relying on one garment alone.

rules.name: Outfit grooming coordination guidance
rules.guideline: Visible grooming choices such as hairstyle, beard and overall neatness should support the visual direction of the outfit.

clean_polished.description: Neat hairstyles and well-maintained facial hair can support structured and polished outfits.

relaxed_casual.description: Natural or relaxed grooming can complement casual outfits when the overall appearance remains intentional.

fashion_forward.description: Distinctive hairstyles or facial-hair styling can support expressive outfits when they reinforce the overall style direction.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing a complete look, consider whether visible grooming supports the outfit's overall style direction.

rules.name: Outfit neckwear coordination guidance
rules.guideline: Ties, scarves and other neckwear should support the outfit through appropriate formality, colour and visual scale.

tie_with_formalwear.description: A tie should complement the shirt, tailoring and overall formal direction rather than appearing disconnected.

scarf_with_casualwear.description: Casual scarves can add texture or colour while supporting the existing outfit rather than competing with it.

statement_neckwear.description: Bold neckwear can become a deliberate accent when the remaining outfit provides enough visual space.

rules.styling_tip: When visible neckwear is present, evaluate its formality, colour and visual prominence against the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit bag coordination guidance
rules.guideline: A visible bag should support the outfit through its function, size, colour, material or style direction.

casual_bags.description: Crossbody bags, backpacks and casual totes can support relaxed everyday outfits.

structured_bags.description: Structured bags can support cleaner and more polished outfits.

statement_bags.description: A distinctive bag can act as a deliberate visual element when the remaining outfit is controlled.

rules.styling_tip: When a bag is visible, consider whether its function and visual character support the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit hat coordination guidance
rules.guideline: A hat or cap should support the outfit's overall style, proportions and occasion rather than appearing unrelated.

casual_caps.description: Baseball caps and similar casual headwear work naturally with relaxed everyday outfits.

structured_headwear.description: More structured headwear can complement outfits with a defined or classic styling direction.

statement_headwear.description: Distinctive hats can become a deliberate focal element when the rest of the outfit remains visually controlled.

rules.styling_tip: When headwear is visible, check whether its style and visual presence support the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit sunglasses coordination guidance
rules.guideline: Sunglasses should support the outfit through frame style, colour, visual weight and occasion.

minimal_frames.description: Simple frames work well when the outfit has a clean, understated visual direction.

bold_frames.description: Distinctive frames can add personality to simple outfits but may compete with already strong visual elements.

frame_colour.description: Frame colour can repeat, complement or intentionally contrast with colours already present in the outfit.
examples: black frames with black-and-white outfits
brown frames with beige-and-brown outfits
metal frames with cool neutral outfits

rules.styling_tip: When sunglasses are visible, evaluate their frame style and visual weight together with the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit watch coordination guidance
rules.guideline: A visible watch should complement the outfit through strap material, case style, visual scale and overall formality.

leather_strap.description: Leather-strap watches generally complement classic and polished outfits, especially when other leather elements are coordinated.

metal_bracelet.description: Metal watches can support clean, modern and refined outfits.

sport_watch.description: Sport-oriented watches naturally suit relaxed, active and contemporary outfits.

visual_scale.description: The watch should look proportionate to the overall styling rather than becoming unintentionally dominant.

rules.styling_tip: When a watch is visible, consider its strap, case style and visual scale in relation to the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit belt coordination guidance
rules.guideline: A visible belt should support the outfit through its formality, material, colour and relationship with the trousers and footwear.

leather_belt.description: Leather belts generally suit polished outfits and can coordinate naturally with leather footwear.

casual_belt.description: Canvas, woven or casual belts can support relaxed outfits without introducing unnecessary formality.

belt_and_footwear.description: For polished outfits, belt and footwear can use similar colour and material families to create visual continuity.
examples: brown leather belt with brown leather loafers
black leather belt with black dress shoes

rules.styling_tip: When a belt is visible, evaluate its material and formality together with the trousers and footwear.

rules.name: Outfit jewelry coordination guidance
rules.guideline: Visible jewelry should support the outfit through metal finish, visual scale and styling direction.

minimal_jewelry.description: Simple chains, rings or bracelets work well when the outfit has a clean and understated direction.

layered_jewelry.description: Multiple jewelry pieces can create a stronger styling statement when their finishes and visual scale remain intentionally coordinated.

metal_finish.description: Using compatible metal finishes can create a more unified appearance, while deliberate mixing can create a contemporary contrast.
examples: silver chain with silver-toned rings
gold chain with gold-toned bracelet
mixed metals used deliberately in a fashion-forward outfit

rules.styling_tip: When jewelry is visible, evaluate the combined metal finish, quantity and visual presence rather than each piece alone.

rules.name: Outfit underwear visibility guidance
rules.guideline: Visible underwear should be intentional and appropriate to the outfit rather than appearing accidentally exposed.

covered.description: Keeping underwear fully covered generally creates a cleaner and more polished appearance.

intentional_visibility.description: If an outfit intentionally includes visible layering underneath, the visible layer should look deliberate and coordinated.

accidental_visibility.description: Unexpected exposure caused by low-rise garments, loose layers or movement can make an outfit appear unfinished.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing an outfit image, distinguish intentional layering from accidental underwear exposure.

rules.name: Traditional and modern outfit balance
rules.guideline: Traditional and contemporary garments can be combined when their proportions, colours and styling details create a deliberate visual relationship.

traditional_base.description: A traditional garment can remain the main visual element while contemporary supporting pieces keep the outfit current.
examples: kurta + tapered trousers + minimal sneakers
kurta + straight trousers + loafers

modern_base.description: A contemporary outfit can incorporate one traditional element to introduce cultural character without making the styling visually disconnected.
examples: minimal shirt + tailored trousers + traditional stole
modern kurta-inspired shirt + straight trousers

balanced_fusion.description: When mixing traditional and modern pieces, keep the overall colour, proportion and formality relationship intentional.

rules.styling_tip: When traditional and modern garments are mixed, evaluate whether both style directions feel intentionally connected.

rules.name: Outfit dress-code transition guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit can be designed to transition between different dress-code levels when key garments or accessories can be changed without rebuilding the entire look.

casual_to_smart.description: Replace casual footwear or an outer layer with a more refined option while keeping the core outfit.
examples: t-shirt + trousers + sneakers → t-shirt + trousers + loafers
casual overshirt → structured jacket

day_to_evening.description: A simple daytime base can transition into an evening look by changing selected accessories, footwear or layering.
examples: daytime sneakers → evening loafers
light overshirt → darker structured jacket

transition_control.description: Keep the core colour and silhouette stable while changing only a few elements to avoid making the transition visually disconnected.

rules.styling_tip: When recommending versatile outfits, identify which single elements can be changed to shift the dress level.

rules.name: Outfit repeat-wear versatility
rules.guideline: Versatile garments should be able to work across multiple outfits without making the overall styling repetitive or visually disconnected.

versatile_base_piece.description: Neutral and adaptable garments can support several combinations by changing the surrounding pieces.
examples: white t-shirt with jeans, beige trousers or olive trousers
navy shirt with beige, grey or white trousers

styling_variation.description: Change footwear, layering, accessories or supporting garments to create a different appearance from the same core piece.

statement_piece_reuse.description: A strong statement garment can be reused effectively when the surrounding colours and supporting pieces change enough to create a distinct combination.

rules.styling_tip: When suggesting outfits, consider whether a garment can create multiple distinct looks with different supporting pieces.

rules.name: Outfit transparency coordination
rules.guideline: Sheer or semi-transparent garments should be layered and styled intentionally so that transparency supports the outfit rather than appearing accidental.

controlled_transparency.description: A slightly transparent garment can work when the underlying layer is intentionally selected and visually coordinated.
examples: sheer shirt + simple neutral inner layer + trousers
lightweight semi-transparent overshirt + plain t-shirt

opaque_base_layer.description: When transparency is noticeable, a clean base layer can provide visual structure and prevent unintended exposure.

intentional_statement.description: Higher transparency can become a deliberate fashion element when the rest of the outfit remains controlled.

rules.styling_tip: When transparency is visible, evaluate whether the underlying layer and amount of transparency look intentional.

rules.name: Outfit cuff and sleeve styling guidance
rules.guideline: Rolled, pushed-up or buttoned sleeves can change the visual character of an outfit and should be used intentionally.

rolled_sleeves.description: Rolling shirt or overshirt sleeves can create a more relaxed and casual appearance.

buttoned_sleeves.description: Keeping sleeves neatly buttoned generally creates a cleaner and more structured appearance.

pushed_up_sleeves.description: Pushing sleeves toward the forearm can create a relaxed styling direction while keeping the garment visually controlled.

rules.styling_tip: When sleeve styling is visible, consider whether the sleeve treatment supports the intended formality and overall style.

rules.name: Shirt open-button styling guidance
rules.guideline: The number of open shirt buttons can change the visual character of an outfit and should suit the intended styling direction.

fully_buttoned.description: A fully buttoned shirt creates a neat and structured appearance.

one_button_open.description: Leaving one upper button open creates a relaxed appearance while keeping the outfit polished.

multiple_buttons_open.description: Opening several upper buttons creates a more relaxed and expressive appearance and works best when intentional.

rules.styling_tip: When a shirt is open at the neckline, consider whether the amount of opening matches the outfit's intended style and occasion.

rules.name: T-shirt tuck styling guidance
rules.guideline: How a T-shirt is tucked can change the outfit's silhouette and should support the intended styling direction.

untucked.description: An untucked T-shirt generally creates a relaxed and effortless appearance.

full_tuck.description: A full tuck creates a cleaner waist definition and can make the outfit appear more structured.

front_tuck.description: A partial front tuck can create visual waist definition while retaining a relaxed appearance.

rules.styling_tip: Choose the T-shirt tuck based on the desired silhouette, outfit direction and relationship with the bottom garment.

rules.name: Outfit shoe lace styling guidance
rules.guideline: Visible shoelaces and their styling can affect the neatness and character of casual footwear.

neat_lacing.description: Clean and secure lacing supports a polished appearance and keeps the footwear visually controlled.

relaxed_lacing.description: Looser or more relaxed lacing can support an intentionally casual or streetwear appearance.

lace_colour.description: Lace colour can either blend with the shoe for a subtle look or create a deliberate accent.
examples: white laces on white sneakers for a clean appearance
contrasting laces used intentionally as a sneaker accent

rules.styling_tip: When laces are clearly visible, evaluate their neatness, looseness and colour as part of the footwear styling.

rules.name: Outfit sleeve layer interaction
rules.guideline: When multiple upper-body layers are worn, their sleeve relationship should look intentional and avoid unnecessary bunching or visual confusion.

clean_sleeve_relationship.description: Inner sleeves should sit naturally under outer sleeves without excessive bunching.

visible_inner_sleeve.description: A deliberately visible inner sleeve can add depth when its colour, length and styling direction support the outer layer.

avoid_excessive_bunching.description: Too much fabric gathered around the arms can make layered outfits appear bulky or unintentional.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing layered outfits, check how the sleeves of each layer interact rather than evaluating each sleeve separately.

rules.name: Outfit collar layer interaction
rules.guideline: When multiple upper-body layers are worn, their collars or neck openings should create a deliberate and visually clear relationship.

clean_collar_relationship.description: Inner and outer collars should remain visually distinct without unnecessary overlapping or collapsing.

visible_inner_collar.description: A visible inner collar can add structure and depth when its shape and colour support the outer layer.

open_neck_layers.description: Open-neck layers can work together when the visible space around the neckline remains intentional and uncluttered.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing layered outfits, check the interaction between neck openings and collars across all visible upper layers.

rules.name: Outfit hem visibility guidance
rules.guideline: Visible hems from layered garments should create intentional visual separation rather than looking accidental or overcrowded.

subtle_hem_visibility.description: A small amount of inner-layer hem showing can add depth while keeping the outfit visually clean.

intentional_long_layer.description: A noticeably longer inner layer can create a deliberate layered silhouette when the length difference is visually controlled.

excessive_hem_overlap.description: Too many visible hems or poorly controlled length differences can make the lower part of layered outfits appear cluttered.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing layered outfits, check the visibility and spacing of each garment hem from top to bottom.

rules.name: Outfit carrying method coordination
rules.guideline: The way a bag or personal item is carried can affect the visual balance and practicality of an outfit.

shoulder_carry.description: Shoulder-carried bags generally keep the outfit visually relaxed and work naturally with casual styling.

crossbody_carry.description: A crossbody position creates a visible diagonal line across the torso and can become part of the outfit's visual structure.

hand_carry.description: Hand-carried structured bags can support a cleaner and more polished appearance.

rules.styling_tip: When a carried item is visible, consider both the item itself and how its position affects the overall outfit.

rules.name: Outfit footwear condition guidance
rules.guideline: The condition of footwear should be appropriate to the overall presentation and can strongly affect how polished the outfit appears.

polished_footwear.description: Clean and well-maintained footwear supports refined and structured outfits.

casual_wear.description: Casual footwear can show normal signs of wear, but excessive dirt or damage can distract from the outfit.

statement_footwear.description: Distinctive footwear should remain visually intentional; poor condition can reduce its intended styling impact.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing an outfit image, assess footwear condition separately because it can change the perceived finish of the complete look.

rules.name: Outfit cultural context guidance
rules.guideline: When an outfit is intended for a culturally specific event, styling should respect the event's expected clothing conventions while allowing appropriate personal expression.

cultural_event.description: Traditional or culturally associated garments can be appropriate when they align with the event context.

modern_traditional_mix.description: Contemporary garments can be combined with traditional elements when the overall styling remains respectful and intentional.
examples: kurta + tailored trousers
traditional jacket + modern trousers
kurta + minimal loafers

context_sensitivity.description: The appropriate level of traditional styling can vary between regions, communities and specific events.

rules.styling_tip: Consider the specific event context before recommending traditional or contemporary clothing combinations.

rules.name: Outfit personal style consistency
rules.guideline: Outfit recommendations should consider the wearer's established personal style so that new pieces feel compatible rather than completely disconnected.

style_signature.description: Repeated preferences in silhouettes, colours, footwear or accessories can form a recognizable personal style direction.
examples: regularly wearing relaxed silhouettes
frequently using neutral colours
preferring minimal sneakers and simple accessories

controlled_experimentation.description: A new trend can be introduced through one or two elements while keeping familiar style elements elsewhere.

style_disconnection.description: A completely different style direction may feel disconnected when none of the existing personal style elements are retained.

rules.styling_tip: When user history or previous outfits are available, use recurring style preferences to guide new recommendations.

rules.name: Outfit garment repetition guidance
rules.guideline: Repeating the same distinctive garment or visual element too many times within one outfit can reduce visual clarity.

single_statement_element.description: One strongly distinctive garment or detail can establish the main visual character of the outfit.
examples: graphic jacket with otherwise simple garments
bold printed trousers with a plain top

controlled_repetition.description: Repeating a subtle element can create continuity, but repeated strong elements should be used intentionally.
examples: one repeated colour across two pieces
matching subtle hardware details

excessive_repetition.description: Multiple highly similar statement elements can make the outfit feel overly themed or visually repetitive.
examples: multiple oversized logo garments
several competing statement accessories

rules.styling_tip: Check how many strong visual elements repeat across the outfit and whether the repetition appears intentional.

rules.name: Outfit negative space guidance
rules.guideline: Intentional empty visual space between garments, accessories and exposed areas can help an outfit feel clearer and less crowded.

clean_negative_space.description: Simple areas without competing details can give strong garments or accessories room to stand out.

accessory_spacing.description: Leaving visual space between prominent accessories can prevent the upper body from appearing unnecessarily crowded.

layer_spacing.description: Controlled gaps between visible layers can make layering easier to read and distinguish.

rules.styling_tip: When analysing an outfit, consider not only what is present but also whether enough visual space remains between strong elements.

rules.name: Outfit social setting guidance
rules.guideline: The same occasion can require different styling depending on whether the setting is intimate, group-oriented, public or highly social.

intimate_setting.description: For dates, dinners or smaller gatherings, refined details and controlled styling can create a more considered appearance.

group_social_setting.description: For larger social gatherings, balanced casual or smart-casual outfits can provide personality while remaining appropriate.

public_active_setting.description: Public outings involving movement or longer periods outside benefit from practical garments and footwear while maintaining the intended style.

rules.styling_tip: When recommending an outfit, consider the social environment and interaction level in addition to the basic occasion.

rules.name: Outfit visual transition guidance
rules.guideline: When one garment has a strong visual difference from another, intermediate elements can help the eye move naturally through the outfit.

colour_transition.description: A middle layer or accessory can visually connect contrasting upper and lower colours.
examples: navy shirt + white sneakers with a neutral belt
black jacket + beige trousers with a white inner layer

material_transition.description: A middle-texture garment can help connect noticeably different materials within a layered outfit.
examples: cotton t-shirt + textured overshirt + denim
smooth shirt + knit layer + tailored trousers

visual_gap.description: A controlled intermediate element can prevent two visually strong garments from competing directly.

rules.styling_tip: Look at how the eye moves from one major garment to another and identify whether an intermediate element improves continuity.

rules.name: Outfit formality bridge guidance
rules.guideline: When garments have different levels of formality, an intermediate piece can help create a more intentional overall dress level.

casual_to_refined.description: A polished intermediate element can connect relaxed garments with more refined pieces.
examples: t-shirt + structured overshirt + tailored trousers
jeans + collared shirt + clean loafers

formal_to_relaxed.description: A casual supporting piece can soften a formal garment while keeping the overall outfit intentional.
examples: blazer + plain t-shirt + clean sneakers
tailored trousers + knit polo + minimal sneakers

balanced_middle.description: Choosing one intermediate-formality garment can prevent the outfit from feeling split between two unrelated dress levels.

rules.styling_tip: When combining garments with different formality levels, identify whether one element successfully bridges the two directions.

rules.name: Outfit symmetry and asymmetry guidance
rules.guideline: Symmetrical styling can create a balanced appearance, while controlled asymmetry can add visual interest without making the outfit feel chaotic.

symmetrical_styling.description: Similar visual weight on both sides can create a clean and balanced appearance.
examples: plain shirt + centered necklace + evenly balanced accessories
structured jacket + simple symmetrical layering

controlled_asymmetry.description: One-sided or uneven visual details can create a deliberate fashion accent.
examples: crossbody bag worn across one side
one prominent bracelet with otherwise minimal accessories

balance.description: If one side has a strong visual element, keep the remaining details simpler so the asymmetry feels intentional.

rules.styling_tip: Use symmetry for a clean appearance and controlled asymmetry when adding a deliberate visual accent.

rules.name: Outfit detail hierarchy guidance
rules.guideline: When an outfit contains several details, they should have different levels of visual importance so the overall look remains clear.

primary_detail.description: Choose one major detail that receives the most visual attention.
examples: graphic shirt + simple trousers + minimal accessories
statement jacket + plain inner layer + simple footwear

secondary_details.description: Supporting details should complement the primary detail without competing with it.
examples: statement sneakers + plain outfit + simple watch
textured overshirt + plain tee + minimal necklace

minimal_support.description: Keep remaining small details restrained when the outfit already has a strong focal element.

rules.styling_tip: Give the outfit one clear primary detail, then reduce competing details around it.

rules.name: Outfit fabric weight balance guidance
rules.guideline: When combining garments with different fabric weights, the overall outfit should maintain a visually and functionally balanced feel.

lightweight_base.description: Light fabrics work well as base layers under moderately heavier outer pieces.
examples: cotton t-shirt + denim overshirt + relaxed trousers
lightweight shirt + structured jacket + tailored trousers

heavy_base.description: Heavier garments can work with simpler and lighter supporting pieces to avoid excessive visual or physical bulk.
examples: heavy knit sweater + lightweight trousers
structured jacket + plain cotton t-shirt + clean trousers

layer_weight_progression.description: In layered outfits, fabric weight can gradually increase toward the outer layer for a natural layering structure.

rules.styling_tip: Balance fabric weight across the outfit so heavier pieces feel intentional rather than unnecessarily bulky.

rules.name: Outfit visual scale guidance
rules.guideline: Large, medium and small visual elements can be combined to create a clear sense of scale across an outfit.

large_element.description: A large visual element can act as the dominant scale reference for the outfit.
examples: oversized jacket + simple trousers + small accessories
large graphic shirt + plain bottoms + minimal footwear

medium_elements.description: Medium-sized details can connect a large garment with smaller accessories.
examples: boxy shirt + regular-width trousers + medium watch
relaxed jacket + straight trousers + medium crossbody bag

small_elements.description: Small accessories and details work best as supporting elements when the outfit already contains large visual pieces.

rules.styling_tip: Mix different visual scales intentionally so large garments, medium pieces and small details do not compete equally.

rules.name: Outfit visual framing guidance
rules.guideline: Details near the face, neckline, waist and footwear can frame the outfit and influence how the overall look is visually read.

upper_frame.description: Necklines, collars, hairstyles and accessories near the face can define the upper visual frame.
examples: open collar + minimal chain + clean hairstyle
crew-neck t-shirt + simple watch + minimal upper details

middle_frame.description: Waist-level elements such as belts, tucks and bags can visually connect the upper and lower parts of an outfit.
examples: tucked shirt + simple belt + straight trousers
untucked tee + crossbody bag + relaxed trousers

lower_frame.description: Trouser hems, socks and footwear can define the finishing frame of the outfit.
examples: cropped trousers + visible socks + clean sneakers
full-length trousers + minimal socks + loafers

rules.styling_tip: Check the visual frames around the face, waist and feet to make sure each area supports the overall outfit.

rules.name: Outfit visual density by zone guidance
rules.guideline: Visual detail can be distributed across the upper, middle and lower outfit zones to prevent one area from becoming unnecessarily crowded.

upper_zone.description: If the upper area contains strong graphics, layers or accessories, keep nearby details controlled.
examples: printed shirt + plain trousers + minimal accessories
layered jacket + plain tee + simple necklace

middle_zone.description: Belts, waist details, tucks and bags can increase visual density around the middle of the outfit.
examples: statement belt + simple upper and lower pieces
crossbody bag + restrained waist details

lower_zone.description: Detailed trousers, visible socks or statement footwear can create stronger visual density near the feet.
examples: cargo trousers + simple top + clean sneakers
plain trousers + statement sneakers + minimal lower details

rules.styling_tip: When one outfit zone becomes visually dense, simplify nearby details to maintain a controlled overall appearance.

rules.name: Outfit visual scale progression guidance
rules.guideline: Visual elements can gradually change in size from one part of the outfit to another to create a more connected overall appearance.

upper_to_lower.description: A large upper garment can transition into medium or smaller visual elements below.
examples: oversized graphic tee + straight trousers + minimal sneakers
boxy overshirt + relaxed trousers + simple footwear

lower_to_upper.description: A statement lower element can be balanced by keeping upper details more controlled.
examples: wide-leg trousers + plain fitted tee + minimal accessories
statement sneakers + simple trousers + clean shirt

layered_progression.description: Different garment sizes across layers can create a deliberate visual progression.

rules.styling_tip: Look for a deliberate change in visual scale from one outfit zone to another rather than making every element equally prominent.

rules.name: Outfit visual restraint guidance
rules.guideline: When an outfit already contains several noticeable elements, reducing additional visual details can keep the overall look intentional.

strong_garment.description: If one garment has a strong design, keep surrounding garments and details relatively restrained.
examples: bold printed shirt + plain trousers + simple sneakers
statement jacket + plain tee + minimal accessories

multiple_details.description: When several noticeable details are already present, avoid adding unnecessary competing elements.
examples: graphic tee + cargo trousers + minimal jewellery
layered outfit + statement sneakers + simple accessories

clean_finish.description: A restrained finishing approach can make the main styling choices easier to notice.

rules.styling_tip: After identifying the outfit's strongest details, remove or simplify anything that does not add useful visual value.

rules.name: Outfit movement practicality guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should allow comfortable movement appropriate to the activity while maintaining its intended silhouette.

active_setting.description: For walking, commuting or active situations, allow sufficient ease through the shoulders, waist, thighs and knees.
examples: relaxed t-shirt + straight trousers + comfortable sneakers
overshirt + relaxed jeans + low-profile sneakers

seated_setting.description: For outfits involving extended sitting, avoid excessive tightness around the waist, hips and thighs.
examples: regular shirt + relaxed trousers + loafers
knit polo + straight trousers + minimal sneakers

formal_setting.description: Structured garments should retain their intended shape without restricting normal movement.

rules.styling_tip: Check whether the outfit remains comfortable and visually consistent during the movements required by the occasion.

rules.name: Outfit temperature comfort guidance
rules.guideline: Clothing choices should provide an appropriate level of warmth or breathability for the expected temperature and environment.

hot_conditions.description: Prefer breathable, lightweight garments and avoid unnecessary heavy layering.
examples: linen shirt + lightweight trousers + breathable sneakers
cotton t-shirt + relaxed trousers + minimal footwear

cool_conditions.description: Add appropriate layers or warmer fabrics while maintaining comfortable movement.
examples: t-shirt + knit layer + trousers
shirt + overshirt + jeans

variable_conditions.description: When temperature may change, use removable layers that allow the outfit to adapt.

rules.styling_tip: Prioritize temperature comfort while keeping removable layers coordinated with the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit functional accessory balance guidance
rules.guideline: Functional accessories should serve a practical purpose while remaining visually compatible with the outfit.

bags.description: Choose a bag size and structure that can carry the required items without overwhelming the outfit.
examples: crossbody bag + casual t-shirt + relaxed trousers
structured work bag + shirt + tailored trousers

headwear.description: Caps and other practical headwear should suit the outfit's overall style and activity.
examples: baseball cap + casual streetwear outfit
simple cap + relaxed travel outfit

utility_items.description: Practical items such as watches, belts or everyday bags should complement rather than unnecessarily compete with the main outfit.

rules.styling_tip: Choose functional accessories based on what you need to carry or use, then keep their style compatible with the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit visual focus position guidance
rules.guideline: The position of a noticeable detail can influence where attention naturally begins when viewing an outfit.

upper_focus.description: Details near the face and upper body can make the outfit feel more top-focused.
examples: statement collar + plain trousers
bold necklace + simple t-shirt and jeans

middle_focus.description: Waist-level details can create a visual stopping point between the upper and lower outfit.
examples: distinctive belt + simple shirt and trousers
tucked shirt + noticeable waist detail

lower_focus.description: Distinctive trousers or footwear can direct attention toward the lower part of the outfit.
examples: statement sneakers + plain trousers and tee
wide-leg trousers + simple upper layers

rules.styling_tip: Place the strongest visual detail where you want attention to begin, then keep surrounding areas supportive.

rules.name: Outfit occasion duration guidance
rules.guideline: For occasions lasting several hours, outfit choices should balance appearance, comfort and durability throughout the expected duration.

short_duration.description: Short events allow more emphasis on visual styling because prolonged comfort is less important.
examples: statement shirt + tailored trousers + loafers
structured jacket + plain tee + clean sneakers

long_duration.description: Long events benefit from breathable fabrics, comfortable footwear and garments that remain presentable over time.
examples: breathable shirt + relaxed trousers + comfortable loafers
lightweight overshirt + straight jeans + supportive sneakers

extended_outdoor.description: Long outdoor activities require greater attention to weather suitability, movement and practical comfort.

rules.styling_tip: When an occasion lasts for many hours, prioritize pieces that remain comfortable and presentable throughout the full duration.

rules.name: Outfit maintenance during wear guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should be styled in a way that remains neat and intentional during normal wear throughout the occasion.

wrinkle_control.description: Choose fabrics and layering approaches that are less likely to create distracting wrinkles during extended wear.
examples: structured overshirt + plain tee + relaxed trousers
knit polo + straight trousers for extended wear

shape_retention.description: Garments should retain their intended shape rather than becoming visibly distorted during normal movement.
examples: structured shirt + straight trousers
well-shaped knitwear + relaxed jeans

neatness.description: Check collars, hems, cuffs and layers periodically when the outfit is worn for a long duration.

rules.styling_tip: Choose garments that can maintain their intended appearance during normal wear instead of requiring constant adjustment.

rules.name: Outfit footwear activity fit guidance
rules.guideline: Footwear should suit the physical demands of the activity while remaining compatible with the outfit's overall styling.

walking.description: For extended walking, prioritize comfortable and supportive footwear with casual or smart-casual outfits.
examples: straight jeans + t-shirt + comfortable sneakers
relaxed trousers + polo + supportive minimal sneakers

formal_activity.description: Formal occasions require footwear that matches the dress level while remaining practical for the expected activity.
examples: tailored trousers + shirt + loafers
suit trousers + formal shirt + dress shoes

active_setting.description: Activities involving significant movement should use footwear designed for that activity rather than prioritizing appearance alone.

rules.styling_tip: Match footwear to both the outfit's dress level and the amount of physical activity expected.

rules.name: Outfit coverage balance guidance
rules.guideline: The amount of skin covered by different garments should create a balanced appearance appropriate to the outfit and setting.

high_coverage.description: Full-length garments across the outfit create a more covered and structured appearance.
examples: full-sleeve shirt + full-length trousers
long-sleeve knitwear + straight jeans

moderate_coverage.description: Combining covered upper layers with shorter or lighter lower pieces can create a balanced casual look.
examples: overshirt + t-shirt + shorts
long-sleeve shirt + tailored shorts

low_coverage.description: When multiple garments expose more skin, keep the overall styling intentional and appropriate to the setting.

rules.styling_tip: Consider the total coverage of the outfit rather than evaluating each garment separately.

rules.name: Outfit occasion practicality guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should account for practical requirements of the occasion without compromising its intended style.

work_setting.description: Choose pieces that allow easy movement, professional presentation and practical daily use.
examples: breathable shirt + tailored trousers + comfortable loafers
polo + chinos + clean minimal sneakers

travel_setting.description: Prioritize comfortable fabrics, practical footwear and layers that can adapt to changing conditions.
examples: t-shirt + overshirt + relaxed trousers + sneakers
polo + lightweight trousers + comfortable sneakers

event_setting.description: For events, combine the required dress level with enough comfort for the expected duration and activity.

rules.styling_tip: Consider what the wearer needs to do during the occasion, not only how the outfit looks.

rules.name: Outfit reversible layer strategy guidance
rules.guideline: When a garment can be worn in more than one orientation or styling configuration, use its reversible or dual-sided design to create coordinated outfit variations.

reversible_outerwear.description: A reversible jacket or overshirt can provide two different visual surfaces while maintaining the same basic outfit.
examples: reversible jacket + plain t-shirt + straight trousers
reversible overshirt + neutral tee + jeans

dual_styling.description: When both sides of a garment are visually different, coordinate the visible side with the rest of the outfit rather than treating both sides identically.
examples: dark outerwear side + light neutral base
patterned outerwear side + plain supporting garments

simplicity.description: Because the garment already provides visual variation, keep other elements relatively controlled.

rules.styling_tip: For reversible garments, choose the visible side first and then coordinate the remaining pieces around that version.

rules.name: Outfit footwear transition guidance
rules.guideline: When changing footwear within the same outfit, the rest of the styling should continue to support the intended overall look.

casual_to_smart.description: Replacing casual sneakers with loafers or other refined footwear can raise the dress level while keeping the clothing coordinated.
examples: plain shirt + trousers + sneakers to loafers
polo + chinos + sneakers to loafers

smart_to_casual.description: Switching refined footwear to clean casual footwear can create a more relaxed version of the same clothing combination.
examples: shirt + tailored trousers + loafers to minimal sneakers
blazer + trousers + dress shoes to clean sneakers

coordination.description: When footwear changes, check whether belt, socks and other visible details still coordinate with the new footwear.

rules.styling_tip: Treat footwear changes as an outfit adjustment and recheck the visible details that visually connect with the shoes.

rules.name: Outfit garment versatility guidance
rules.guideline: Versatile garments can be styled across multiple dress levels and occasions when their surrounding pieces are changed appropriately.

basic_garments.description: Simple neutral garments can support different outfit directions through changes in footwear, layering and accessories.
examples: plain white t-shirt + jeans + sneakers for casual
plain white t-shirt + blazer + tailored trousers for smart-casual

layering_variation.description: Adding or removing an outer layer can change the visual character of the same base outfit.
examples: plain tee + trousers + sneakers
same base + structured overshirt + loafers

wardrobe_value.description: Garments that coordinate with multiple existing pieces can create more outfit combinations without requiring many additional items.

rules.styling_tip: When evaluating a garment, consider how many different outfit directions it can support with simple changes around it.

rules.name: Outfit colour reversal guidance
rules.guideline: Reversing the dominant and supporting colours of a familiar combination can create a noticeably different outfit while preserving colour compatibility.

dominant_colour_swap.description: A colour that was previously used as a supporting element can become the dominant garment colour.
examples: black shirt + beige trousers
beige shirt + black trousers

light_dark_reversal.description: Swapping which colour occupies the larger visual area can change the perceived balance of the same colour pairing.
examples: navy top + white trousers
white top + navy trousers

styling_control.description: When reversing a colour combination, keep footwear and accessories relatively neutral so the changed colour distribution remains clear.

rules.styling_tip: If a colour pairing already works, try reversing which colour dominates the outfit before introducing a completely new palette.

rules.name: Outfit garment interchangeability guidance
rules.guideline: When two garments serve a similar styling role, replacing one with another can preserve the outfit's overall direction while changing its character.

upper_body_swap.description: Similar-role tops can be exchanged while keeping the lower half and overall colour direction coordinated.
examples: plain t-shirt replaced with a knit polo
casual shirt replaced with a lightweight overshirt

lower_body_swap.description: Similar-role bottoms can be exchanged to alter the silhouette or dress level while retaining the upper-body concept.
examples: straight jeans replaced with relaxed trousers
chinos replaced with tailored trousers

footwear_swap.description: Footwear can be exchanged to shift the outfit's character without rebuilding the entire combination.

rules.styling_tip: When replacing a garment, preserve its styling role first, then reassess colour, proportion and formality.

rules.name: Outfit layer visibility control guidance
rules.guideline: In layered outfits, the amount of each layer that remains visible can be adjusted to control how strongly each garment contributes to the overall look.

minimal_visibility.description: Keep the base layer mostly covered when the outer garment is intended to remain the primary visual element.
examples: overshirt + mostly covered plain t-shirt + trousers
jacket + minimally visible inner layer + jeans

balanced_visibility.description: Allow controlled portions of the inner layer to remain visible so both garments contribute to the outfit.
examples: open overshirt + visible t-shirt + relaxed trousers
open jacket + visible shirt + straight trousers

strong_inner_layer.description: A distinctive inner layer can remain more visible when the outer garment is used mainly as a supporting layer.

rules.styling_tip: Adjust how much of each layer is visible based on which garment you want to contribute more strongly to the final look.

rules.name: Outfit layer opening guidance
rules.guideline: The way an outer garment is opened or closed can change the visual structure and perceived casualness of a layered outfit.

fully_open.description: An open outer layer creates clear separation between the inner garment and outer garment.
examples: open overshirt + plain t-shirt + trousers
open casual jacket + tee + jeans

partially_open.description: A partially closed layer creates a more structured appearance while retaining some visibility of the inner garment.
examples: partially buttoned overshirt + tee + relaxed trousers
partially zipped jacket + plain inner layer + jeans

fully_closed.description: A closed outer layer creates a cleaner and more contained silhouette.

rules.styling_tip: Choose the layer opening based on the desired visual structure, temperature and amount of inner-layer visibility.

rules.name: Outfit footwear profile guidance
rules.guideline: The visual profile of footwear should complement the proportions and character of the garments rather than feeling disconnected from them.

bulky_footwear.description: Chunkier footwear can work with relaxed or wider garments that have enough visual presence to support the shoe profile.
examples: wide-leg trousers + chunky sneakers
baggy jeans + substantial sneakers

slim_footwear.description: Slimmer footwear generally integrates more naturally with streamlined or narrower garment silhouettes.
examples: straight trousers + minimal sneakers
tailored trousers + sleek loafers

profile_consistency.description: The shoe shape should feel intentional alongside the visual character of the trousers and overall outfit.

rules.styling_tip: Compare the visual profile of the footwear with the garment silhouettes before finalizing the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment flexibility guidance
rules.guideline: Garment flexibility should suit the movement and activity required by the occasion while preserving the intended outfit appearance.

high_flexibility.description: Stretch or naturally flexible garments can support activities requiring frequent movement.
examples: stretch trousers + knit polo + sneakers
flexible jeans + cotton t-shirt + casual sneakers

structured_garments.description: Structured garments can create a sharper appearance but should retain enough ease for normal movement.
examples: structured blazer + relaxed trousers
structured overshirt + straight jeans

mixed_flexibility.description: Combining flexible base garments with structured outer pieces can balance comfort and visual structure.

rules.styling_tip: Match garment flexibility to the amount of movement expected rather than choosing structure or stretch based on appearance alone.

rules.name: Outfit footwear grounding guidance
rules.guideline: Footwear can visually anchor an outfit by providing a stable finishing element that connects the lower body to the overall styling direction.

neutral_grounding.description: Neutral footwear can visually stabilize outfits containing stronger colours, patterns or layers.
examples: bold printed shirt + plain trousers + white sneakers
colourful overshirt + neutral trousers + black sneakers

tonal_grounding.description: Footwear that repeats or complements a lower-outfit colour can create a more connected visual finish.
examples: brown trousers + brown loafers
black trousers + black sneakers

statement_grounding.description: Statement footwear can become a deliberate finishing element when the rest of the outfit provides enough visual space.

rules.styling_tip: Use footwear either as a neutral anchor or as a deliberate finishing statement, depending on the rest of the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit visual continuity guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit can feel more cohesive when related visual characteristics are repeated or gradually carried from one garment to another.

colour_continuity.description: Repeating a related colour family across separate outfit elements can create a connected appearance.
examples: navy shirt + navy-toned sneakers
brown belt + brown footwear

shape_continuity.description: Related garment shapes can create a smoother visual flow across the outfit.
examples: relaxed overshirt + relaxed trousers
structured shirt + straight tailored trousers

detail_continuity.description: Small repeated details can connect otherwise separate garments without making the outfit overly matched.

rules.styling_tip: Look for one or two visual characteristics that naturally continue through the outfit instead of matching every element.

rules.name: Outfit occasion change adaptability guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit can be planned to adapt when the wearer's setting changes during the same day.

day_to_evening.description: A simple daytime base can transition to an evening setting by changing or adding selected pieces.
examples: plain tee + trousers + sneakers with an overshirt added for evening
polo + chinos with loafers replacing casual sneakers

casual_to_social.description: A casual base can become more suitable for a social setting through a refined layer or accessory.
examples: t-shirt + jeans + sneakers with a structured jacket added
casual shirt + trousers with refined footwear

adaptable_base.description: Neutral and versatile base garments make transitions between different settings easier.

rules.styling_tip: When the setting may change, build the outfit around a versatile base and plan one or two easy transition changes.

rules.name: Outfit garment layer compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Garments should be compatible in construction and wearability when layered together so that the combination remains comfortable and visually clean.

base_layer.description: Base garments should sit comfortably underneath the next layer without excessive bunching or restriction.
examples: plain t-shirt + lightweight overshirt
thin shirt + structured jacket

middle_layer.description: A middle layer should have enough room to accommodate the base layer while remaining compatible with the outer garment.
examples: t-shirt + knit cardigan + relaxed jacket
shirt + lightweight knit + coat

outer_layer.description: The outermost garment should accommodate the layers underneath without pulling, distortion or unnecessary bulk.

rules.styling_tip: Before combining layers, check whether each garment can comfortably accommodate the layer underneath without losing its intended shape.

rules.name: Outfit garment occasion reuse guidance
rules.guideline: A versatile garment can be reused across different occasions by changing the supporting pieces while preserving its core styling identity.

same_top_different_settings.description: A single top can move between casual and refined settings when paired with different bottoms and footwear.
examples: plain polo + jeans + sneakers for casual
same polo + tailored trousers + loafers for smart-casual

same_bottom_different_settings.description: A versatile bottom can support different occasions through changes in the upper layer and footwear.
examples: straight trousers + t-shirt + sneakers for casual
same trousers + shirt + loafers for refined styling

repeat_strategy.description: Changing supporting elements can make a frequently worn garment feel visually different without requiring a completely new outfit.

rules.styling_tip: Reuse versatile garments by changing their supporting pieces rather than repeating the exact same complete combination.

rules.name: Outfit garment function matching guidance
rules.guideline: Each garment should support the practical function required by the outfit rather than being selected only for appearance.

protection.description: Outer garments should provide appropriate protection from wind, rain or cooler conditions when required.
examples: water-resistant jacket + trousers + sneakers for rainy travel
warm coat + knit layer + trousers for cold weather

breathability.description: Garments for warm conditions should allow airflow and avoid unnecessary insulation.
examples: linen shirt + lightweight trousers
cotton t-shirt + relaxed lightweight pants

utility.description: Garments with functional features should match situations where those features are genuinely useful.

rules.styling_tip: Choose garments according to what they need to do in the situation, then coordinate their appearance with the rest of the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Garments with compatible construction, styling language and intended use generally combine more naturally within the same outfit.

construction.description: Garments with compatible structural characteristics can create a more coherent combination.
examples: structured blazer + tailored trousers
relaxed overshirt + relaxed jeans

styling_language.description: Pieces that communicate a similar design direction can work together without requiring identical details.
examples: minimal shirt + minimal trousers + clean sneakers
utility overshirt + cargo trousers + practical sneakers

intended_use.description: Garments designed for very different purposes may require a deliberate bridge before being combined.

rules.styling_tip: Before combining two pieces, check whether their construction, design language and intended use can coexist naturally.

rules.name: Outfit occasion backup option guidance
rules.guideline: When an outfit depends on a specific garment or accessory, having a coordinated backup option can preserve the intended style if that item becomes unsuitable.

footwear_backup.description: Keep an alternative pair that maintains a similar dress level and colour direction.
examples: loafers with clean minimal sneakers as an alternative
brown sneakers with white sneakers as an alternative

layer_backup.description: A removable outer layer can provide an alternative when temperature or setting changes unexpectedly.
examples: overshirt as backup for a cooler evening
lightweight jacket as backup for changing weather

style_continuity.description: The backup should work with the existing outfit rather than requiring a complete change.

rules.styling_tip: For situations with uncertainty, prepare one coordinated backup piece that can replace the most change-sensitive part of the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment scalability guidance
rules.guideline: A garment's styling impact can change depending on how much of it is visible and what other pieces surround it.

statement_piece.description: When a garment is intended to be the main visual element, surrounding pieces should provide enough visual space for it to stand out.
examples: statement overshirt + plain tee + simple trousers
bold trousers + neutral top + minimal footwear

supporting_piece.description: A visually distinctive garment can function as a supporting element when partially covered or paired with a stronger focal piece.
examples: printed shirt under a plain jacket
textured knit under a structured overshirt

adaptability.description: Changing visibility or surrounding pieces can change the role of the same garment without replacing it.

rules.styling_tip: Consider whether each garment is acting as the main statement or a supporting element, then adjust its visibility accordingly.

rules.name: Outfit garment pairing by occasion guidance
rules.guideline: Garment combinations should reflect the expected level of interaction and movement associated with the occasion.

social_casual.description: Relaxed garments can be paired with approachable footwear and simple accessories for informal social settings.
examples: boxy t-shirt + straight jeans + clean sneakers
casual shirt + relaxed trousers + minimal sneakers

semi_formal.description: A structured upper garment combined with refined but comfortable lower pieces can suit semi-formal interaction.
examples: knit polo + tailored trousers + loafers
overshirt + collared shirt + straight trousers

formal.description: Formal interaction generally benefits from coordinated structured garments and refined footwear.

rules.styling_tip: Consider the social setting and expected interaction when deciding how structured or relaxed the garment pairing should be.

rules.name: Outfit photography readability guidance
rules.guideline: When an outfit is being photographed or shown online, garment details should remain visually readable without excessive visual interference.

detail_visibility.description: Important garment features should remain visible rather than being hidden by overlapping layers or accessories.
examples: keep a distinctive shirt print visible in outfit photos
avoid covering the main jacket detail with a large bag

background_separation.description: Choose a visually simple background when garment details need to be clearly seen.
examples: dark outfit against a lighter simple background
light outfit against a darker simple background

pose_and_display.description: The outfit should be displayed in a way that allows its silhouette, layers and key details to be understood.

rules.styling_tip: When presenting an outfit visually, make sure the important garments and styling details remain easy to identify.

rules.name: Outfit colour context guidance
rules.guideline: The perceived appearance of an outfit colour can change depending on surrounding colours, lighting and the visual environment.

surrounding_colour.description: A colour may appear stronger, softer or different when placed beside contrasting or similar colours.
examples: cream can appear warmer beside brown
grey can appear cooler beside blue

lighting_context.description: Warm or cool lighting can influence how garment colours are perceived.
examples: cream under warm indoor lighting
white under cool daylight

visual_environment.description: The surrounding environment should be considered when evaluating whether an outfit colour combination appears balanced.

rules.styling_tip: Evaluate important colour decisions in the lighting and environment where the outfit will actually be worn or viewed.

rules.name: Outfit cost-per-wear value guidance
rules.guideline: A garment's practical wardrobe value can be considered by how frequently and across how many situations it can be worn.

high_reuse.description: Basic versatile garments can provide greater practical value when they work with many existing wardrobe pieces.
examples: plain white t-shirt styled with jeans, trousers and shorts
neutral overshirt used across casual and smart-casual outfits

limited_use.description: Highly distinctive garments may have fewer styling opportunities and should be considered as statement additions rather than everyday basics.
examples: bold patterned jacket
occasion-specific festive kurta

wardrobe_balance.description: A wardrobe can combine frequently reusable basics with a smaller number of distinctive pieces.

rules.styling_tip: When evaluating a new garment, consider how many existing outfits and occasions it can realistically support.

rules.name: Outfit packing efficiency guidance
rules.guideline: When preparing outfits for travel, combinations should maximize the number of looks from a limited number of garments.

base_garments.description: Choose versatile neutral garments that can coordinate with multiple tops, bottoms and footwear options.
examples: black trousers with multiple neutral and coloured tops
white sneakers with several casual outfits

layer_reuse.description: Outer layers that work across multiple combinations can reduce the number of garments needed.
examples: neutral overshirt worn over different t-shirts
lightweight neutral jacket paired with multiple trousers

footwear_efficiency.description: A small selection of versatile footwear can cover multiple planned outfits.
examples: white sneakers for several casual combinations
brown loafers for multiple smart-casual combinations

rules.styling_tip: For travel, build combinations around versatile pieces that can create multiple distinct looks without overpacking.

rules.name: Outfit formality signal balance
rules.guideline: When garments send different formality signals, combine them intentionally so the overall outfit feels cohesive.

formal_anchor.description: A clearly formal garment can anchor an outfit while more relaxed pieces soften the overall appearance.
examples: blazer + plain t-shirt + clean sneakers
dress shirt + relaxed trousers + minimal sneakers

casual_anchor.description: A casual main piece can be elevated with cleaner, more structured supporting garments.
examples: plain t-shirt + tailored trousers + loafers
overshirt + clean trousers + minimal leather shoes

mixed_signals.description: Avoid combining too many unrelated formality signals unless the contrast is deliberate.

rules.styling_tip: Identify the strongest formality signal in the outfit and make the remaining pieces support or intentionally balance it.

rules.name: Outfit seated appearance guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should remain visually balanced and practical when the wearer sits, especially during extended periods or seated activities.

top_position.description: Tops should remain appropriately positioned when sitting without excessive bunching or unwanted exposure.
examples: t-shirt with sufficient length for seated movement
shirt that stays appropriately positioned when sitting

trouser_behavior.description: Trousers should maintain comfortable coverage and a clean appearance while seated.
examples: trousers with enough rise for comfortable sitting
jeans that do not excessively pull across the waist when seated

layer_behavior.description: Jackets and overshirts should remain manageable when sitting and should not create unnecessary bulk.
examples: unstructured jacket for extended sitting
overshirt that remains comfortable when seated

rules.styling_tip: Consider how the complete outfit behaves while sitting, not only how it looks while standing.

rules.name: Outfit mobility range guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should allow the level of movement required by the activity without restricting normal body movement.

upper_body_movement.description: Shirts, jackets and layered tops should allow sufficient movement through the shoulders and arms.
examples: relaxed overshirt for active casual movement
jacket with enough arm mobility for commuting

lower_body_movement.description: Trousers and shorts should provide enough ease for walking, stairs and other expected movements.
examples: relaxed trousers for travel
comfortable shorts for outdoor activities

activity_matching.description: The required movement level should influence garment selection and overall outfit construction.

rules.styling_tip: Match garment mobility to the actual movement demands of the occasion rather than choosing fit based only on appearance.

rules.name: Outfit visual balance with logo guidance
rules.guideline: Visible logos should support the outfit's overall visual balance without competing with the main styling elements.

small_logo.description: Small logos generally integrate easily without becoming a major visual element.
examples: small chest logo on a plain t-shirt
subtle logo on a cap with a simple outfit

large_logo.description: Large or prominent logos can become a major visual element and should be balanced by simpler surrounding pieces.
examples: large graphic logo + plain trousers + minimal sneakers
bold branded hoodie + simple bottoms and accessories

multiple_logos.description: Several prominent logos can create competing visual elements and may reduce outfit clarity.

rules.styling_tip: Treat a prominent logo as part of the outfit's visual design and keep competing elements controlled.

rules.name: Outfit button and zipper coordination
rules.guideline: Visible buttons, zippers and other garment closures can contribute to the outfit's overall visual character and should work cohesively with the surrounding pieces.

metal_finish.description: Visible metal closures can coordinate with other visible hardware or accessories when a consistent finish is desired.
examples: silver zipper + silver watch
dark metal zipper + black accessories

closure_visibility.description: When closures are visually prominent, simpler surrounding garments can prevent excessive detail.
examples: utility jacket with visible zippers + plain t-shirt
overshirt with prominent buttons + minimal accessories

style_context.description: Closure details can reinforce the character of casual, utility, streetwear or tailored outfits.

rules.styling_tip: Treat prominent buttons and zippers as design details and coordinate them with the outfit's overall visual language.

rules.name: Outfit eyewear frame coordination
rules.guideline: Eyewear frame shape, size and visual weight should complement the outfit rather than compete with its overall styling.

frame_size.description: Frame size should feel proportionate to the wearer's face and the visual weight of the outfit.
examples: minimal outfit + medium lightweight frames
bold streetwear + stronger frame design

frame_shape.description: Frame shapes can reinforce or contrast with the overall styling direction.
examples: rounded frames with relaxed casual styling
angular frames with structured modern outfits

frame_visual_weight.description: Heavy frames can become a noticeable focal element, so other accessories may be kept simpler.

rules.styling_tip: Choose eyewear that supports the outfit's visual character while remaining proportionate to the face and other accessories.

rules.name: Outfit footwear sole proportion guidance
rules.guideline: The thickness and visual weight of a shoe sole should work with the proportions and silhouette of the rest of the outfit.

thin_sole.description: Slim soles generally pair naturally with cleaner, narrower or more refined silhouettes.
examples: slim trousers + low-profile sneakers
tailored trousers + loafers

thick_sole.description: Chunkier soles create more visual weight and can complement relaxed or oversized silhouettes.
examples: baggy jeans + chunky sneakers
oversized streetwear + platform-style sneakers

proportion_balance.description: A very heavy sole with a very slim outfit can create an exaggerated visual imbalance, while an extremely slim shoe under very wide trousers may look visually light.

rules.styling_tip: Match footwear sole weight to the visual volume of the trousers and overall outfit silhouette.

rules.name: Outfit buttoning choice guidance
rules.guideline: The number of visible buttons left open or closed can change the perceived formality, openness and visual character of an outfit.

fully_buttoned.description: A fully buttoned shirt generally creates a cleaner and more structured appearance.

partially_open.description: Leaving one or two upper buttons open can create a more relaxed appearance while maintaining a polished look.

layered_shirting.description: An open shirt or overshirt can reveal the inner layer and create additional visual depth.
examples: open overshirt + plain t-shirt
open casual shirt + neutral inner layer

rules.styling_tip: Adjust shirt buttoning according to the desired formality, occasion and layering effect.

rules.name: Outfit visual asymmetry guidance
rules.guideline: Intentional asymmetry can add visual interest when one side of an outfit carries a noticeable detail or styling difference.

uneven_layering.description: An intentionally uneven layer position can create a relaxed and fashion-forward appearance.
examples: open overshirt with one side naturally overlapping
asymmetrical outer layer over a simple base

single_side_detail.description: A detail concentrated on one side can create a subtle visual point without requiring multiple statement elements.
examples: crossbody bag worn across one side
single visible bracelet or cuff detail

balance.description: When asymmetry is strong, surrounding garments should remain controlled so the difference looks intentional rather than accidental.

rules.styling_tip: Use asymmetry deliberately and keep the rest of the outfit controlled enough for the uneven detail to look intentional.

rules.name: Outfit repeatable base guidance
rules.guideline: A simple base outfit can serve as a consistent foundation while different layers or accessories change the final styling direction.

simple_base.description: Plain, well-fitting base garments make it easier to create different looks without changing the entire outfit.
examples: plain white t-shirt + neutral trousers
plain black t-shirt + dark jeans

styling_variation.description: The same base can take on different visual directions through outer layers, footwear or accessories.
examples: white t-shirt + beige trousers + sneakers for casual
white t-shirt + beige trousers + loafers + blazer for elevated styling

wardrobe_foundation.description: Repeatable base combinations can simplify daily outfit planning and support a more versatile wardrobe.

rules.styling_tip: Build reliable base combinations first, then change one or two supporting elements to create a different outfit direction.

rules.name: Outfit accessory removability guidance
rules.guideline: Accessories should be easy to remove or reduce when the outfit needs to shift toward a simpler or more practical appearance.

core_outfit.description: The main garments should remain visually complete even after optional accessories are removed.
examples: plain shirt + trousers should work without a necklace
casual outfit should remain balanced without a cap

optional_details.description: Watches, chains, bracelets, sunglasses and similar details can be treated as adjustable styling layers.
examples: remove sunglasses when moving indoors
remove a statement chain for a cleaner setting

adaptability.description: A removable accessory setup allows the same outfit to adapt to changing settings without replacing the main garments.

rules.styling_tip: Make sure the outfit works on its own, then use accessories as adjustable layers rather than essential structural elements.

rules.name: Outfit occasion duration guidance
rules.guideline: The expected duration of an occasion can influence garment comfort, layering choices and footwear practicality.

short_duration.description: For brief occasions, visual styling can take greater priority when extended comfort is less important.
examples: short dinner outing with structured footwear
brief event with a statement outer layer

long_duration.description: For extended occasions, breathable layers, comfortable footwear and manageable garment construction become more important.
