examples: long wedding event with comfortable formal footwear
extended travel day with lightweight layers

planning.description: The longer the occasion lasts, the more important it becomes to balance appearance with sustained comfort.

rules.styling_tip: Consider how long the outfit will be worn and balance visual styling with comfort for the full duration.

rules.name: Indoor-outdoor outfit transition guidance
rules.guideline: Outfits that move between indoor and outdoor environments should remain practical and visually coherent across both settings.

layer_management.description: A removable outer layer can help adapt the outfit when moving between different environments.
examples: t-shirt + lightweight overshirt for indoor-outdoor movement
shirt + light jacket for changing environments

footwear_practicality.description: Footwear should remain suitable for both the expected indoor setting and outdoor conditions.
examples: clean sneakers for casual indoor and outdoor use
loafers for indoor events with manageable outdoor movement

visual_continuity.description: The outfit should still look complete after removing an outer layer when entering a warmer indoor environment.

rules.styling_tip: Build the outfit so removing or adding an outer layer does not disrupt the overall look.

rules.name: Outfit colour memory guidance
rules.guideline: Repeating a subtle colour element across different parts of an outfit can make the overall combination easier to visually connect and remember.

subtle_repetition.description: A small repeated colour detail can create a recognizable connection without requiring identical garments.
examples: brown watch with brown shoes
white sneakers with a small white garment detail

statement_colour.description: When an outfit contains a distinctive colour, repeating a small amount of that colour elsewhere can integrate it into the complete look.
examples: burgundy shirt with a subtle burgundy accessory
olive overshirt with a small olive detail

restraint.description: Colour repetition should remain subtle when the outfit already contains several noticeable visual elements.

rules.styling_tip: Use small repeated colour details to create visual connections without making every accessory match exactly.

rules.name: Outfit garment maintenance level guidance
rules.guideline: The maintenance requirements of garments should be considered when building practical outfits for regular wear.

low_maintenance.description: Easy-care garments are generally more practical for frequent use, commuting and travel.
examples: machine-washable cotton t-shirt for everyday wear
easy-care trousers for regular commuting

high_maintenance.description: Garments requiring special care may be better suited to occasions where their maintenance needs are manageable.
examples: dry-clean-only blazer for formal events
delicate knitwear for planned occasions

outfit_planning.description: Combining several high-maintenance garments can increase the overall care required for the outfit.

rules.styling_tip: Consider the care required by each garment when choosing outfits for repeated or practical use.

rules.name: Outfit visual scale relationship guidance
rules.guideline: Large, medium and small visual elements should relate to each other so the outfit does not feel unintentionally dominated by one scale.

large_elements.description: Large garments or graphics can be balanced with simpler medium or smaller supporting elements.
examples: oversized graphic t-shirt + simple trousers + minimal sneakers
large statement jacket + understated inner layer

small_elements.description: Small accessories and details can add refinement without competing with larger garments.
examples: minimal watch with oversized casual styling
small chain with a plain fitted shirt

overall_relationship.description: Mixing different visual scales can create interest when the hierarchy is intentional.

rules.styling_tip: Balance large, medium and small visual elements so one scale does not unintentionally dominate the entire outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment age consistency guidance
rules.guideline: The visible wear and age of garments should feel reasonably consistent when combined in one outfit.

condition_matching.description: A heavily worn garment can look disconnected when paired with exceptionally crisp and new-looking pieces.
examples: heavily faded jeans + similarly relaxed casual pieces
crisp new trousers + well-maintained shirt and shoes

intentional_contrast.description: Different garment ages can work when the contrast is part of the intended style.
examples: vintage denim + clean modern t-shirt
distressed jacket + minimal contemporary trousers

overall_condition.description: Visible damage, excessive fading or worn footwear should be considered separately from intentional vintage or distressed styling.

rules.styling_tip: Check whether differences in garment age look intentional and stylistically connected rather than accidental.

rules.name: Outfit hardware visual noise guidance
rules.guideline: Multiple prominent hardware details can increase visual complexity, so metal and utility elements should be balanced across the outfit.

hardware_density.description: Several visible zippers, buckles, rings, chains and metal details can compete for attention.
examples: utility jacket + minimal accessories
multiple rings + simple clothing hardware

hardware_repetition.description: Repeating a similar hardware finish can create cohesion when several metal details are visible.
examples: silver zipper + silver watch
dark metal buckles + dark metal accessories

visual_control.description: When one garment already contains substantial hardware, simpler supporting pieces can keep the outfit visually controlled.

rules.styling_tip: Treat prominent hardware as part of the outfit's visual detail level and avoid unnecessary competition between metal elements.

rules.name: Outfit garment repair visibility guidance
rules.guideline: Visible repairs, alterations or mending details can affect the visual character of an outfit and should appear intentional when they are noticeable.

subtle_repair.description: Small, clean repairs that remain visually unobtrusive generally integrate easily into everyday outfits.
examples: neatly repaired inner seam
subtle stitching repair on a casual garment

visible_repair.description: Prominent patches or contrasting repairs can become design elements and should work with the garment's overall style.
examples: visible patch on vintage denim
contrasting repair detail on workwear

intentionality.description: Unplanned damage can look different from deliberate distressed or patched styling.

rules.styling_tip: Distinguish intentional repair or distressed details from accidental damage when evaluating the outfit's overall appearance.

rules.name: Outfit scent coordination
rules.guideline: Fragrance choice should complement the occasion, environment and overall styling without becoming overwhelming.

daytime.description: Fresh, clean and lighter fragrance profiles generally suit daytime and warm environments.
examples: fresh citrus fragrance with summer casual wear
clean aquatic fragrance with everyday outfits

evening.description: Deeper or warmer fragrance profiles can suit evening settings when used appropriately.
examples: woody fragrance with smart-casual evening wear
warm spicy fragrance for a dinner outfit

intensity.description: Fragrance intensity should remain appropriate for the environment and social setting.

rules.styling_tip: Match fragrance character and intensity to the occasion and environment rather than treating it as a fixed outfit accessory.

rules.name: Hair and neckline balance guidance
rules.guideline: Hairstyle volume and shape can influence how open, structured or visually balanced a neckline appears.

open_necklines.description: Open necklines can provide visual space around the neck and may work well with hairstyles that keep the face and neckline relatively clear.
examples: open collar shirt + clean hairstyle
crew-neck t-shirt + controlled hairstyle volume

high_necklines.description: Higher necklines create more visual structure around the upper body, so hairstyle volume can be considered accordingly.
examples: mock neck + controlled side-volume hairstyle
high-neck knitwear + clean structured hairstyle

overall_balance.description: Hair, neckline and upper-body details should work together without creating excessive visual concentration around the face and neck.

rules.styling_tip: Consider hairstyle volume together with neckline openness when balancing the upper portion of an outfit.

rules.name: Outfit seam detail guidance
rules.guideline: Prominent seam lines and contrasting stitching can add visual structure and should be considered when balancing detailed garments.

contrast_stitching.description: Contrasting stitching can become a noticeable design element, especially on denim and workwear.
examples: dark denim with contrasting stitching + simple top
workwear jacket with visible stitching + plain trousers

minimal_seams.description: Clean tonal seams generally create a quieter visual appearance and work well with other detailed pieces.
examples: minimal jacket + statement accessory
tonal trousers + graphic top

detail_balance.description: Several garments with prominent seam details can increase visual complexity when combined.

rules.styling_tip: Treat contrasting seam lines as visible design details when assessing the outfit's overall visual complexity.

rules.name: Outfit label detail guidance
rules.guideline: Visible garment labels, tags or label-like branding can add small visual elements that affect an otherwise clean outfit.

subtle_labels.description: Small tonal labels generally create minimal visual distraction.
examples: small tonal label on a plain hoodie
subtle woven label on an overshirt

prominent_labels.description: Large or contrasting labels can become noticeable design elements and may work best with simpler surrounding pieces.
examples: large back label + plain trousers
contrasting woven label + minimal accessories

visual_control.description: When multiple garments contain prominent labels, the combined effect can increase visual detail.

rules.styling_tip: Consider visible labels as part of the outfit's total visual detail rather than ignoring them as minor garment features.

rules.name: Outfit garment surface uniformity guidance
rules.guideline: The visual uniformity of garment surfaces can influence whether an outfit appears clean, textured or intentionally varied.

uniform_surfaces.description: Smooth and visually consistent garment surfaces generally create a cleaner and more streamlined appearance.
examples: smooth cotton t-shirt + clean trousers
plain knitwear + smooth tailored trousers

varied_surfaces.description: Combining noticeably different surface characteristics can add visual interest when the variation is intentional.
examples: textured knit + smooth trousers
brushed overshirt + clean cotton t-shirt

surface_balance.description: Several highly textured surfaces can make an outfit feel visually busy, while completely uniform surfaces may appear very minimal.

rules.styling_tip: Use surface variation deliberately to decide whether the outfit should feel streamlined or more texturally expressive.

rules.name: Outfit garment scale consistency guidance
rules.guideline: The apparent scale of garment details should feel intentional across the outfit, especially when mixing subtle and oversized design elements.

small_details.description: Small collars, pockets and subtle details generally work naturally with clean, minimal garments.
examples: small collar + minimal trousers
subtle pocket details + clean sneakers

large_details.description: Large collars, oversized pockets or prominent garment features can become visual anchors and benefit from simpler supporting pieces.
examples: large utility pockets + plain inner layer
oversized collar + simple trousers

consistency.description: Mixing detail scales can work when the difference appears deliberate rather than accidental.

rules.styling_tip: Check whether garment detail sizes feel intentionally related across the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment edge softness guidance
rules.guideline: The visual softness or sharpness of garment edges can influence whether an outfit feels relaxed, structured or intentionally contrasted.

soft_edges.description: Draped or softly structured garments can create a relaxed visual character.
examples: soft knitwear + relaxed trousers
draped overshirt + casual denim

structured_edges.description: Sharp garment edges and structured construction can create a cleaner and more formal appearance.
examples: structured blazer + tailored trousers
crisp shirt + pressed trousers

mixed_edges.description: Combining soft and structured pieces can create intentional contrast when their proportions remain compatible.

rules.styling_tip: Use the contrast between soft and structured garment edges deliberately to influence the outfit's overall character.

rules.name: Outfit garment opacity consistency guidance
rules.guideline: The opacity and visual coverage of garments should be considered when combining layers so unexpected transparency does not disrupt the outfit.

opaque_base.description: Opaque base garments provide predictable coverage and work well under most layers.
examples: opaque t-shirt under an open overshirt
opaque shirt under a lightweight jacket

semi_transparent_layers.description: Semi-transparent garments can intentionally reveal the underlying layer but require deliberate coordination.
examples: lightweight sheer overshirt over a tonal inner layer
semi-transparent summer shirt over a simple vest

coverage_balance.description: When transparency is noticeable, the underlying garment should support the intended visual effect.

rules.styling_tip: Consider what becomes visible through lightweight or semi-transparent garments before finalizing the layered combination.

rules.name: Outfit garment closure visibility guidance
rules.guideline: Whether garment closures are visible or concealed can change the visual simplicity and structure of an outfit.

concealed_closures.description: Hidden buttons, zippers or fasteners generally create a cleaner and more streamlined appearance.
examples: concealed zip jacket + minimal trousers
hidden-button shirt + clean smart-casual styling

visible_closures.description: Visible closures can add structure or utilitarian detail and may become part of the garment's visual identity.
examples: visible zip jacket + simple inner layer
button-front overshirt + plain t-shirt

overall_detail.description: Closure visibility should be considered together with other garment details when controlling visual complexity.

rules.styling_tip: Treat visible closures as design elements and concealed closures as tools for a cleaner visual appearance.

rules.name: Outfit garment drape direction guidance
rules.guideline: The direction and fall of fabric can influence how movement and visual flow are perceived across the outfit.

vertical_drape.description: Longer garments with vertical fabric fall can create a continuous downward visual flow.
examples: long overshirt over straight trousers
long coat over a simple monochrome base

relaxed_drape.description: Soft, relaxed fabric fall can reinforce an easygoing silhouette.
examples: relaxed shirt + loose trousers
soft knitwear + wide-leg trousers

structured_drape.description: More controlled fabric fall can support sharper and more structured styling.
examples: structured blazer + tailored trousers
crisp shirt + straight trousers

rules.styling_tip: Consider how fabric naturally falls and whether its direction supports the intended silhouette of the complete outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment layer friction guidance
rules.guideline: Layered garments should interact comfortably without excessive bunching, catching or unwanted movement between fabric surfaces.

smooth_layers.description: Smooth inner and outer layers generally move more easily against each other.
examples: cotton t-shirt + lightweight overshirt
smooth shirt + structured jacket

high_friction_layers.description: Rough or cling-prone fabric combinations can create bunching or restrict natural movement.
examples: textured knit + rough inner fabric
heavy fleece + tightly fitted outer layer

layer_management.description: When multiple layers are used, each layer should have enough room to sit naturally over the one underneath.

rules.styling_tip: Check how fabrics interact when layered instead of judging each garment independently.

rules.name: Outfit garment static cling guidance
rules.guideline: Static cling can change how lightweight garments sit against the body or other layers and should be considered when relevant.

lightweight_fabrics.description: Thin synthetic or lightweight fabrics can sometimes cling to the body or adjacent layers.
examples: lightweight trousers with a smooth inner layer
thin shirt over a fitted base

layer_effect.description: Unexpected cling can change the intended drape and visual appearance of a layered outfit.

rules.styling_tip: Consider static-prone fabrics when a clean drape or smooth layering effect is important.

rules.name: Outfit garment shrinkage consideration
rules.guideline: Expected garment shrinkage can affect fit, proportions and coordination after washing or repeated care.

natural_fibres.description: Some natural-fibre garments may change dimensions after washing depending on fabric construction and care.
examples: cotton t-shirt becoming shorter after washing
wool knitwear changing size when improperly washed

fit_planning.description: Potential dimensional changes should be considered when evaluating a garment's intended fit.

care_label.description: Following the garment's recommended care method helps reduce unexpected changes in fit and proportion.

rules.styling_tip: Consider post-wash dimensions when selecting or evaluating garments whose fit depends on precise length or proportion.

rules.name: Outfit garment fade consistency guidance
rules.guideline: Differences in fading between garments can influence whether an outfit appears coordinated, vintage or unintentionally mismatched.

similar_fade.description: Garments with comparable levels of colour wear can create a cohesive relaxed appearance.
examples: faded denim + washed casual overshirt
washed black jeans + muted graphic t-shirt

contrast_fade.description: A heavily faded statement garment can work with cleaner pieces when the contrast appears intentional.
examples: distressed light denim + crisp white shirt
washed black jeans + clean neutral jacket

colour_control.description: When fading is visually strong, the remaining colour palette can be kept controlled to maintain clarity.

rules.styling_tip: Decide whether differences in garment fading should blend together or intentionally create contrast.

rules.name: Outfit garment pilling control guidance
rules.guideline: Visible fabric pilling can affect the perceived neatness of an outfit, particularly on knitwear and frequently worn garments.

minimal_pilling.description: Well-maintained garments with minimal visible pilling generally maintain a cleaner appearance.

visible_pilling.description: Heavy pilling can make an otherwise coordinated outfit appear less maintained.
examples: pilled sweater with tailored trousers
pilled cardigan over a crisp shirt

maintenance.description: Regular garment care can help maintain the intended surface appearance of knitwear and other prone fabrics.

rules.styling_tip: Check visible fabric pilling when assessing whether an outfit looks intentionally relaxed or simply poorly maintained.

rules.name: Outfit garment stretch recovery guidance
rules.guideline: Garments should retain their intended shape after normal movement and wear rather than becoming noticeably distorted.

shape_retention.description: Garments with good recovery maintain their original silhouette after stretching during normal movement.
examples: stretch trousers returning to their intended shape
ribbed knitwear maintaining its neckline after wear

high_stress_areas.description: Repeated stretching around knees, elbows, waist or seat can affect garment appearance over time.

rules.styling_tip: Consider whether a garment maintains its intended fit after normal movement and repeated wear.

rules.name: Outfit garment colour bleeding guidance
rules.guideline: Colour transfer between garments can alter their intended appearance and should be considered when combining or maintaining contrasting pieces.

dark_garments.description: Strongly dyed dark garments can sometimes transfer colour during washing or when exposed to moisture.
examples: dark denim with light garments
deep black garment with white fabric

maintenance.description: Appropriate washing and care can help preserve the intended colour relationship between garments.

outfit_effect.description: Unexpected colour transfer can reduce the visual cleanliness of high-contrast combinations.

rules.styling_tip: Consider colour-transfer risk when maintaining outfits that combine strongly contrasting garment colours.

rules.name: Outfit garment odour management guidance
rules.guideline: Garment freshness can affect the overall presentation of an outfit, particularly after repeated wear, heat or physical activity.

freshness.description: Clean and appropriately aired garments generally support a more polished overall presentation.

repeated_wear.description: Garments exposed to sweat, humidity or prolonged wear may require appropriate cleaning or airing before reuse.

fabric_consideration.description: Different fabrics can retain odour differently, so care should reflect the material and usage.

rules.styling_tip: Treat garment freshness as part of overall outfit presentation, especially in warm weather or after extended wear.

rules.name: Outfit garment shape recovery guidance
rules.guideline: A garment's ability to recover its intended shape after hanging, folding or normal wear affects how consistently the outfit appears.

structured_garments.description: Structured pieces benefit from maintaining their intended shape between wears.
examples: blazer retaining its shoulder structure
collared shirt retaining its intended collar shape

soft_garments.description: Soft garments may naturally relax or change shape, but excessive distortion can affect the intended silhouette.
examples: knitwear retaining its general body shape
t-shirt maintaining its intended neckline

rules.styling_tip: Check whether garments recover their intended shape between wears before judging the consistency of an outfit.

rules.name: Outfit garment surface wear guidance
rules.guideline: Visible surface wear such as abrasion, fuzzing or roughened areas can change the perceived condition and character of a garment.

controlled_wear.description: Intentional surface wear can contribute to vintage, workwear or distressed styling.
examples: intentionally faded denim
worn-in workwear jacket

unintentional_wear.description: Unexpected abrasion or surface damage can make an otherwise polished outfit appear less maintained.
examples: heavy abrasion on a formal trouser
unexpected fuzzing on a clean knit layer

overall_condition.description: Surface wear should be interpreted in relation to the garment's intended style rather than automatically treated as negative.

rules.styling_tip: Distinguish intentional worn-in character from accidental surface damage when evaluating garment condition.

rules.name: Outfit thermal layering guidance
rules.guideline: Layering should provide appropriate warmth without creating unnecessary bulk or restricting movement.

base_layer.description: A close-to-body base layer can provide warmth while keeping the outer silhouette controlled.
examples: thermal inner + shirt + jacket
lightweight base layer + knitwear

mid_layer.description: The middle layer should add warmth while leaving enough room for the outer garment.
examples: t-shirt + lightweight knit + jacket
thermal inner + overshirt + coat

bulk_control.description: Too many thick layers can create excessive volume and reduce comfort.

rules.styling_tip: Build warmth progressively from thinner inner layers to thicker outer layers while keeping the final silhouette controlled.

rules.name: Outfit garment breathability guidance
rules.guideline: Fabric breathability should match the temperature, activity level and layering needs of the outfit.

warm_conditions.description: Breathable fabrics can help improve comfort in warm conditions.
examples: linen shirt + relaxed trousers
lightweight cotton t-shirt + breathable trousers

layering.description: Breathable inner layers can help prevent excessive heat buildup when multiple garments are worn.

activity.description: Higher activity levels generally increase the importance of breathable garment choices.

rules.styling_tip: Match fabric breathability to weather and activity rather than focusing only on the outfit's appearance.

rules.name: Outfit garment water resistance guidance
rules.guideline: Weather exposure should influence outer-garment selection when rain or moisture is expected.

light_rain.description: A water-resistant outer layer can provide practical protection during light rain while maintaining the outfit underneath.
examples: water-resistant lightweight jacket + casual base
water-resistant overshirt + trousers

heavy_exposure.description: Stronger weather protection may require garments specifically designed for prolonged moisture exposure.

layer_protection.description: The outermost layer should provide the primary weather barrier when protection is required.

rules.styling_tip: Choose the outermost garment according to expected moisture exposure while keeping the underlying outfit practical.

rules.name: Outfit garment packability guidance
rules.guideline: For travel or changing conditions, garments that can be packed and carried efficiently can improve outfit practicality.

packable_layers.description: Lightweight layers that compress reasonably well can be useful when conditions change during the day.
examples: lightweight overshirt carried for evening
compact windbreaker for unpredictable weather

bulk_control.description: Bulky garments can take significant luggage or carrying space and should be planned accordingly.

wrinkle_awareness.description: Packability should be considered alongside how the garment behaves after being folded or compressed.

rules.styling_tip: When carrying extra layers, prioritize pieces that provide useful coverage without creating unnecessary bulk.

rules.name: Outfit reflective detail guidance
rules.guideline: Reflective or highly light-catching garment details can become strong visual elements and should be balanced with the rest of the outfit.

subtle_reflection.description: Small reflective details can add interest without dominating the outfit.
examples: subtle reflective piping on a jacket
small reflective logo on casual outerwear

strong_reflection.description: Large reflective surfaces can become a major visual element and work best with simpler surrounding pieces.
examples: reflective jacket + plain trousers
high-shine outerwear + minimal accessories

context.description: Reflective details can be especially noticeable under artificial or low-light conditions.

rules.styling_tip: Treat reflective details as visual accents and keep competing elements controlled when they are prominent.

rules.name: Outfit stain visibility guidance
rules.guideline: Light and highly uniform garments can make visible stains more noticeable, while darker or textured garments can visually hide minor marks better.

recommendations.styling_tip: For travel, commuting, or messy environments, consider colours and textures that are less visually sensitive to minor stains.

rules.name: Fabric snag compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Delicate or loosely constructed fabrics can catch on rough surfaces and hardware, so outfit combinations should consider how garments interact physically.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid pairing delicate outer layers with rough bags, exposed hardware, or abrasive accessories when durability matters.

rules.name: Outfit drying practicality guidance
rules.guideline: Garments with different drying requirements can affect outfit practicality, especially during humid weather, travel, or frequent washing.

recommendations.styling_tip: For travel or humid conditions, combine lightweight garments that are easier to wash and dry.

rules.name: Outfit stain-prone zone guidance
rules.guideline: Garments around the collar, cuffs, pockets, and lower hems can experience more visible dirt during everyday wear.

recommendations.styling_tip: When frequent cleaning is inconvenient, use more forgiving colours or fabrics around commonly exposed areas.

rules.name: Fabric abrasion tolerance guidance
rules.guideline: Areas that repeatedly rub against seats, bags, straps, or other garments can show wear faster depending on fabric construction.

recommendations.styling_tip: For daily commuting or heavy-use outfits, favour durable fabrics in high-friction areas.

rules.name: Fabric temperature response guidance
rules.guideline: Different fabrics can feel warmer or cooler depending on their structure, weight, and air movement.

recommendations.styling_tip: Choose fabric characteristics according to weather rather than relying only on garment colour.

rules.name: Fabric absorbency guidance
rules.guideline: Fabric absorbency affects how garments handle sweat and moisture and can influence comfort during warm or humid conditions.

recommendations.styling_tip: For hot conditions, consider breathable and moisture-managing fabrics based on activity level.

rules.name: Fabric transparency under lighting guidance
rules.guideline: Thin or light-coloured fabrics can appear more transparent under strong daylight or direct lighting.

recommendations.styling_tip: Check lightweight light-coloured garments under strong lighting before wearing them for formal or public settings.

rules.name: Fabric pucker control guidance
rules.guideline: Uneven tension around seams, buttons, or fitted areas can create puckering that affects the garment's visual finish.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid garments showing excessive puckering because it can make an otherwise well-coordinated outfit look poorly fitted.

rules.name: Fabric crease behaviour guidance
rules.guideline: Some fabrics develop visible creases quickly while others maintain a smoother appearance during extended wear.

recommendations.styling_tip: For long days, travel, or formal events, consider crease behaviour when selecting garments.

rules.name: Fabric compression recovery guidance
rules.guideline: Garments can temporarily lose their smooth shape after prolonged compression from sitting, folding, or carrying bags.

recommendations.styling_tip: For long travel or extended sitting, consider fabrics that recover their appearance easily.

rules.name: Fabric heat retention guidance
rules.guideline: Fabric construction and trapped air can affect how much body heat an outfit retains.

recommendations.styling_tip: For temperature-sensitive outfits, consider heat retention alongside garment thickness and layering.

rules.name: Fabric light reflection guidance
rules.guideline: Fabric surfaces can reflect different amounts of light, changing how prominent a garment appears visually.

recommendations.styling_tip: When one garment has a highly reflective surface, keep surrounding pieces visually controlled.

rules.name: Garment pressure mark guidance
rules.guideline: Tight straps, belts, or layered garments can leave temporary pressure marks or distort the appearance of softer fabrics.

recommendations.styling_tip: Match accessory pressure and layering choices to the fabric's structure when maintaining a clean appearance matters.

rules.name: Fabric snag direction guidance
rules.guideline: Loose fibres, loops, or raised surface textures can catch more easily when exposed to repeated directional contact.

recommendations.styling_tip: Keep raised or delicate fabric surfaces away from repeated contact points when durability is important.

rules.name: Footwear activity suitability guidance
rules.guideline: Footwear should match the physical demands of the activity while remaining visually consistent with the outfit.

recommendations.styling_tip: Prioritize practical footwear for high-movement activities while maintaining the outfit's overall style direction.

rules.name: Bag capacity suitability guidance
rules.guideline: The size of a bag should reasonably match what needs to be carried without overpowering the outfit.

recommendations.styling_tip: Choose bag capacity according to the day's requirements rather than selecting size only for appearance.

rules.name: Pocket accessibility guidance
rules.guideline: Pocket placement and accessibility can affect how practical an outfit feels during everyday movement.

recommendations.styling_tip: For active days, consider whether essential items can be accessed comfortably without disturbing the outfit's appearance.

rules.name: Layer removal sequence guidance
rules.guideline: Layered outfits should remain visually coherent when outer garments are removed during changes in temperature or setting.

recommendations.styling_tip: Build each visible layer so the outfit still looks intentional after removing one or more outer layers.

rules.name: Footwear replacement flexibility guidance
rules.guideline: A well-planned outfit can remain cohesive when footwear is changed to suit comfort, weather, or occasion.

recommendations.styling_tip: When building versatile outfits, choose clothing colours and proportions that can support more than one suitable footwear option.

rules.name: Outfit front-back coherence guidance
rules.guideline: An outfit should remain visually intentional from both front and back views, especially when outerwear, bags, or layered garments change the rear appearance.

recommendations.styling_tip: Check whether the outfit still looks balanced when viewed from behind rather than judging only the front.

rules.name: Outfit side-view coherence guidance
rules.guideline: Side-view appearance can reveal proportion relationships between the chest, waist, hips, garment lengths, and footwear that are less obvious from the front.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use the side view to check whether garment lengths and overall proportions transition naturally.

rules.name: Garment contact-point interaction guidance
rules.guideline: Where two garments repeatedly touch or overlap, their textures, thicknesses, and construction can affect the overall appearance and comfort.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid combinations where overlapping garments bunch, fight for space, or create unnecessary bulk.

rules.name: Accessory interruption guidance
rules.guideline: Accessories should add function or visual interest without unnecessarily interrupting important garment lines, graphics, or structural details.

common_interruption_points: necklace hidden by a high neckline
belt competing with a strong waistband detail
recommendations.styling_tip: Position accessories so they complement rather than unnecessarily obscure key garment details.

rules.name: Outfit detail visibility priority guidance
rules.guideline: When several garments contain useful design details, their visibility should be balanced so important elements are not unnecessarily hidden.

recommendations.styling_tip: Before adding another layer or accessory, check whether it hides a detail that contributes significantly to the outfit.

rules.name: Garment size-label consistency guidance
rules.guideline: Size labels can vary between brands and garment categories, so the labelled size should not be treated as a universal indicator of actual fit.

recommendations.styling_tip: Judge the garment by its actual measurements and intended silhouette rather than relying only on S, M, L, or XL labels.

rules.name: Tailoring allowance guidance
rules.guideline: Some garments can be altered more easily than others, so purchase decisions should consider whether the desired fit can realistically be achieved through tailoring.

recommendations.styling_tip: Prefer garments that already fit critical structural areas correctly because major structural alterations can be difficult or expensive.

rules.name: Fabric colour transfer risk guidance
rules.guideline: Some strongly dyed garments can transfer colour through moisture or friction, potentially affecting lighter garments worn with them.

recommendations.styling_tip: When combining dark heavily dyed garments with light pieces, consider colour-transfer risk during the first few wears.

rules.name: Garment seating compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Some garments change shape or comfort significantly when sitting, especially around waistbands, hems, pleats, and fitted areas.

recommendations.styling_tip: For long seated periods, choose garments that maintain comfort and a clean appearance in both standing and seated positions.

rules.name: Garment movement-noise guidance
rules.guideline: Certain fabrics, hardware, and layered garments can create noticeable sound during movement, which may affect practicality in quiet environments.

recommendations.styling_tip: For offices, libraries, formal events, or quiet environments, consider garments and accessories that remain unobtrusive during movement.

rules.name: Garment measurement consistency guidance
rules.guideline: When combining garments from different brands, their labelled sizes may differ even when the intended fit is similar.

recommendations.styling_tip: Compare actual garment measurements across brands when building a coordinated outfit instead of assuming identical size labels fit the same way.

rules.name: Garment shrinkage compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Different garments can shrink differently after washing, potentially changing their original proportions relative to each other.

recommendations.styling_tip: Follow care instructions and consider expected shrinkage when buying close-fitting or precisely proportioned garments.

rules.name: Garment colour fading compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Garments can fade at different rates through washing, sunlight, and wear, which may gradually change the visual relationship between pieces.

recommendations.styling_tip: For frequently repeated combinations, consider whether the garments are likely to age visually at different rates.

rules.name: Garment care compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Garments requiring very different cleaning methods may be less convenient to maintain as a frequently worn combination.

recommendations.styling_tip: For repeat-wear outfits, consider whether the pieces can be maintained conveniently without creating excessive care requirements.

rules.name: Garment storage compatibility guidance
rules.guideline: Different garment structures require different storage methods to preserve their shape and appearance.

recommendations.styling_tip: Store garments according to their construction so the intended fit and silhouette remain consistent over time.

rules.name: Outfit visual occlusion guidance
rules.guideline: When part of a garment is hidden by another garment, a bag, arms, or the camera angle, the AI should avoid treating the hidden area as confirmed information.

recommendations.styling_tip: Only use clearly visible garment details as confirmed evidence and mark hidden details as uncertain.

rules.name: Outfit analysis confidence guidance
rules.guideline: AI outfit analysis should distinguish between clearly visible information and uncertain visual interpretations.

lower_confidence: exact fit when the full silhouette is not visible
recommendations.styling_tip: Do not present uncertain visual observations as definite facts.

rules.name: Mirror-image handling guidance
rules.guideline: Mirror selfies can reverse the apparent left-right position of garments, accessories, logos, or styling details.

recommendations.styling_tip: Analyse the outfit based on garment characteristics rather than assuming left-right placement in a mirror image represents the real-world orientation.

rules.name: Camera perspective distortion guidance
rules.guideline: Camera distance, lens perspective, and shooting angle can make some garments or body proportions appear different from their real-world appearance.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid making strong fit or proportion conclusions from perspective-distorted images alone.

rules.name: Outfit lighting colour-shift guidance
rules.guideline: Indoor lighting, coloured lights, shadows, and camera white balance can change how garment colours appear in an image.

common_effects: warm indoor light making white appear cream
cool light making colours appear bluer
strong shadows making dark colours appear deeper
recommendations.styling_tip: When colour identification is uncertain, consider lighting conditions before making a precise colour-matching recommendation.

rules.name: Image resolution adequacy guidance
rules.guideline: Low-resolution images can make small garment details, textures, patterns, and accessories difficult to identify reliably.

recommendations.styling_tip: Reduce confidence in fine-grained outfit analysis when image resolution does not clearly show the relevant details.

rules.name: Image blur handling guidance
rules.guideline: Motion blur or focus blur can hide garment edges, patterns, and accessory details and should reduce analysis certainty.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not infer precise garment details from areas that are visibly blurred.

rules.name: Full-body visibility guidance
rules.guideline: A complete outfit assessment is more reliable when the top, bottom, and footwear are visible together.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid making conclusions about unseen garments or the complete silhouette.

rules.name: Pattern recognition confidence guidance
rules.guideline: Small, blurred, or partially hidden patterns can be difficult to identify accurately from an outfit image.

recommendations.styling_tip: If the pattern cannot be confidently identified, describe it generically rather than inventing a specific pattern type.

rules.name: Accessory visibility confidence guidance
rules.guideline: Small accessories should only be identified when their shape and placement are sufficiently visible in the image.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not assume an accessory is present simply because a small unclear object appears near the relevant area.

rules.name: Pose-dependent garment appearance guidance
rules.guideline: A garment can appear tighter, looser, shorter, or differently shaped depending on the person's pose.

common_pose_effects: raised arms shortening visible shirt length
seated posture changing jacket and trouser shape
recommendations.styling_tip: Consider the person's pose before making precise conclusions about garment fit or length.

rules.name: Garment fold interpretation guidance
rules.guideline: Natural fabric folds do not automatically indicate poor fit because folds can result from movement, posture, fabric structure, or layering.

recommendations.styling_tip: Evaluate repeated structural signs rather than judging fit from a single temporary fold.

rules.name: Body-position occlusion guidance
rules.guideline: Arms, crossed legs, turned shoulders, and other body positions can hide important garment areas from the camera.

recommendations.styling_tip: Treat hidden garment areas as unknown instead of estimating their construction or fit.

rules.name: Garment movement-state guidance
rules.guideline: A garment photographed during movement may temporarily appear different from its normal resting position.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use the garment's stable visible structure rather than temporary movement-related distortion for styling analysis.

rules.name: Garment construction versus styling choice guidance
rules.guideline: Visible garment details should be distinguished from temporary styling choices such as rolled sleeves, folded hems, open buttons, or tucked fabric.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not treat a temporary styling adjustment as the garment's permanent construction.

rules.name: Outfit crop boundary handling guidance
rules.guideline: When a garment extends beyond the image frame, the AI should not assume its complete shape, length, or styling details.

recommendations.styling_tip: Treat cropped garment sections as incomplete evidence and avoid precise conclusions about unseen areas.

rules.name: Background colour interference guidance
rules.guideline: Strongly coloured backgrounds can visually influence the perceived colour of nearby garments, especially under unusual lighting.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use neutral reference areas or multiple visual cues when precise garment colour identification is important.

rules.name: Reflective surface interference guidance
rules.guideline: Mirrors, glass, metallic surfaces, and other reflections can introduce duplicated or altered visual information in an outfit image.

recommendations.styling_tip: Distinguish the actual person and garments from reflected or duplicated visual elements before analysing the outfit.

rules.name: Outfit shadow occlusion guidance
rules.guideline: Strong shadows can hide garment details or make colours and textures appear darker than they actually are.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not interpret shadow-darkened areas as definite garment colours or details without sufficient visual evidence.

rules.name: Outfit image angle consistency guidance
rules.guideline: Different camera angles can change the apparent proportions and visibility of the same outfit.

recommendations.styling_tip: When multiple images are available, compare consistent garment features across views before making detailed styling conclusions.

rules.name: Outfit recommendation priority guidance
rules.guideline: When multiple styling improvements are possible, prioritize changes that have the largest practical or visual impact.

recommendations.styling_tip: Address the most impactful issue first instead of overwhelming the user with many minor corrections.

rules.name: Minimal-change styling strategy
rules.guideline: If an outfit already works reasonably well, prefer small targeted improvements instead of replacing multiple garments.

recommendations.styling_tip: Preserve successful parts of the outfit and recommend only changes that meaningfully improve the result.

rules.name: Styling alternative guidance
rules.guideline: When a garment or combination is not ideal for the intended use, provide practical alternatives rather than stopping at criticism.

recommendations.styling_tip: Explain what to change and provide a usable alternative that follows the same overall style direction.

rules.name: Recommendation confidence wording guidance
rules.guideline: AI styling advice should communicate certainty appropriately when recommendations depend on incomplete visual information or subjective preferences.

conditional_language: if you prefer a cleaner look
recommendations.styling_tip: Use direct language for clear observations and conditional language for subjective or uncertain recommendations.

rules.name: Recommendation explanation guidance
rules.guideline: A useful styling recommendation should explain the practical or visual reason behind the suggested change.

recommendations.styling_tip: Give a short reason for each meaningful recommendation so the user understands how the change improves the outfit.

rules.name: User preference preservation guidance
rules.guideline: Styling recommendations should consider the user's stated preferences instead of automatically replacing them with generic fashion conventions.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use the user's preferences as constraints when generating outfit recommendations.

rules.name: Recommendation constraint handling guidance
rules.guideline: When the user provides specific constraints, recommendations should satisfy those constraints before adding optional styling suggestions.

recommendations.styling_tip: Treat explicit user constraints as requirements rather than optional preferences.

rules.name: Budget-aware styling guidance
rules.guideline: When the user specifies a budget, recommendations should prioritize changes that fit within that budget.

recommendations.styling_tip: Prefer using existing suitable pieces before suggesting multiple new purchases.

rules.name: Existing wardrobe prioritization guidance
rules.guideline: When the user asks for styling help using their existing wardrobe, recommendations should prioritize combinations of available garments.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not recommend buying a new item when an appropriate existing wardrobe option can solve the styling need.

rules.name: Recommendation context retention guidance
rules.guideline: Follow-up styling recommendations should retain relevant context already provided by the user unless the user changes it.

recommendations.styling_tip: Maintain relevant constraints across follow-up questions so the user does not need to repeat them.

rules.name: Recommendation actionability guidance
rules.guideline: Styling advice should translate observations into clear actions the user can realistically apply.

recommendations.styling_tip: Prefer specific actionable advice over vague statements such as 'make it better' or 'style it differently'.

rules.name: Reason-to-action connection guidance
rules.guideline: Each significant styling observation should lead to a relevant action that directly addresses the identified issue.

examples: low contrast → add a contrasting element
excessive visual complexity → simplify accessories
occasion mismatch → change the formality level
poor proportion → adjust garment choice or styling
recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid suggesting changes that do not address the actual reason identified in the analysis.

rules.name: Recommendation uncertainty boundary guidance
rules.guideline: When important information is unavailable, the AI should limit the scope of its recommendation instead of filling gaps with assumptions.

recommendations.styling_tip: State what is uncertain and make the recommendation only from information that is sufficiently supported.

rules.name: Recommendation personalization depth guidance
rules.guideline: Recommendations can become more personalized when relevant information about the user's preferences, occasion, comfort, and available wardrobe is known.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use available user context to refine recommendations without inventing personal information that was not provided.

rules.name: Recommendation output prioritization guidance
rules.guideline: The final response should present the most useful recommendations first and keep lower-impact suggestions secondary.

recommendations.styling_tip: Lead with the changes that matter most instead of giving every possible suggestion equal emphasis.

rules.name: Recommendation follow-up refinement guidance
rules.guideline: When a user provides new information after an initial recommendation, the AI should refine the existing advice instead of restarting without context.

recommendations.styling_tip: Update only the affected parts of the recommendation while preserving still-relevant context.

rules.name: Recommendation contradiction control guidance
rules.guideline: Related styling recommendations should remain logically consistent and should not recommend opposing actions without explaining the different conditions.

recommendations.styling_tip: If two recommendations apply under different conditions, clearly explain the condition that changes the advice.

rules.name: Recommendation option diversity guidance
rules.guideline: When multiple outfit options are requested, each option should provide a meaningfully different styling direction rather than minor variations of the same combination.

recommendations.styling_tip: Make alternatives genuinely distinct while keeping them suitable for the user's stated requirements.

rules.name: Recommendation trade-off guidance
rules.guideline: Some styling choices improve one aspect of an outfit while changing another, so relevant trade-offs should be explained.

recommendations.styling_tip: Mention the main trade-off when it could materially affect the user's choice.

rules.name: Recommendation fallback handling guidance
rules.guideline: If the ideal styling option cannot be achieved with the available information or garments, provide the closest practical alternative.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid forcing an unsuitable recommendation when the preferred option is not realistically available.

rules.name: Knowledge-base relevance filtering guidance
rules.guideline: AI should use only knowledge-base rules that are relevant to the garments, colours, fit, occasion, and styling question being analysed.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not apply unrelated knowledge-base rules merely because they are available.

rules.name: Knowledge-base rule priority guidance
rules.guideline: When several knowledge-base rules apply, prioritize rules that directly address the user's main styling problem.

recommendations.styling_tip: Use highly relevant rules first and treat secondary rules as supporting information.

rules.name: Knowledge-base conflict handling guidance
rules.guideline: When two applicable styling rules appear to conflict, AI should consider their conditions before combining or choosing between them.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not blindly combine conflicting rules; identify which condition is more relevant to the current request.

rules.name: Knowledge-base evidence matching guidance
rules.guideline: A knowledge-base rule should be applied only when the visual analysis provides enough evidence that its conditions are present.

recommendations.styling_tip: Do not trigger a specific rule from an assumed garment, colour, fit, or occasion that has not been sufficiently established.

rules.name: Knowledge-base coverage gap guidance
rules.guideline: If the knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently relevant rule, AI should recognize the coverage gap instead of pretending that an exact rule exists.

recommendations.styling_tip: Accuracy is more important than forcing an unsupported knowledge-base conclusion.

rules.name: Knowledge-base rule combination guidance
rules.guideline: Multiple relevant rules can be combined when they address different aspects of the same outfit without creating conflicting recommendations.

recommendations.styling_tip: Combine complementary rules when together they provide a more complete styling recommendation.

rules.name: Knowledge-base duplicate suppression guidance
rules.guideline: When multiple retrieved rules communicate substantially the same styling principle, AI should avoid repeating the same recommendation.

recommendations.styling_tip: Merge overlapping guidance into one clear recommendation instead of repeating similar points.

rules.name: Knowledge-base rule specificity guidance
rules.guideline: When both a general rule and a more specific applicable rule are available, the specific rule should provide the primary guidance.

recommendations.example: A specific rule for navy trousers and beige footwear can take priority over a broad neutral-colour rule when both apply.
recommendations.styling_tip: Use general rules as supporting context when a more specific relevant rule exists.

rules.name: Knowledge-base contextual adaptation guidance
rules.guideline: A general fashion rule may need contextual adjustment based on occasion, weather, activity, and the user's stated preferences.

recommendations.styling_tip: Treat knowledge-base rules as contextual guidance rather than absolute instructions.

rules.name: Knowledge-base recommendation traceability guidance
rules.guideline: Important styling recommendations should be traceable to the relevant visual observation, user requirement, or knowledge-base rule.

recommendations.styling_tip: Avoid recommendations that cannot be connected to any available evidence or relevant styling rule.

rules.name: outfit_visual_depth_layers
rules.guideline: Layered outfits should create visible depth between garments without making the outfit look crowded.
recommendations: Use clearly separated layers such as t-shirt, overshirt and outerwear.
Avoid layers with nearly identical colours and lengths that visually merge.
Keep at least one layer visually dominant.
rules.styling_tip: Layers tab best lagte hain jab har layer clearly distinguish ho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_edge_overlap
rules.guideline: Overlapping garment edges should remain visually intentional so the outfit does not look accidentally stacked.
recommendations: Keep layer overlaps clean around the waist, cuffs and neckline.
Avoid excessive fabric bunching where two garments meet.
Use controlled overlap when creating a relaxed layered look.
rules.styling_tip: Garments ke edges clean overlap karein, random bunching avoid karein.

rules.name: outfit_garment_scale_transition
rules.guideline: When garment volumes change from one piece to another, the transition should look deliberate rather than abrupt.
recommendations: Pair a very wide top with a controlled or intentionally wide bottom.
Avoid combining extreme volume changes without a clear silhouette purpose.
Use footwear volume that supports the overall transition.
rules.styling_tip: Top se bottom tak volume ka transition smooth rakho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_overlap_visibility
rules.guideline: When garments overlap, enough of each important piece should remain visible to communicate the intended outfit.
recommendations: Do not completely hide a key layering piece.
Keep collars, hems or sleeves visible when they are part of the styling.
Reduce unnecessary overlap when it removes the visual identity of a garment.
rules.styling_tip: Layering piece ko itna hide mat karo ki uska purpose hi disappear ho jaye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_volume_transition
rules.guideline: Garment volume should transition naturally across the outfit so the silhouette feels connected from top to bottom.
recommendations: Consider shoulder, torso and leg volume together.
Avoid isolated oversized or extremely narrow pieces unless intentionally styled.
Use footwear shape to support the final silhouette.
rules.styling_tip: Overall silhouette ko ek connected shape ki tarah evaluate karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_scale_by_body_zone
rules.guideline: Garment volume should be considered across upper, middle and lower body zones rather than judging each piece independently.
recommendations: Compare shoulder volume with torso volume.
Compare torso volume with trouser volume.
Avoid an isolated extreme volume in one body zone unless intentionally styled.
rules.styling_tip: Sirf ek garment ka fit nahi, poore body zones ka volume dekho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_boundary_clarity
rules.guideline: Adjacent garments should have enough visual separation to make their individual boundaries understandable.
recommendations: Use contrast in colour, texture or edge position when layers visually merge.
Avoid nearly identical garment tones and overlapping edges when separation is important.
Keep important garment boundaries visible in layered outfits.
rules.styling_tip: Do layers visually merge ho rahe hain to colour ya texture se separation create karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_visual_weight_shift
rules.guideline: When one garment carries significantly more visual weight, the rest of the outfit should support rather than compete with it.
recommendations: Use simpler surrounding pieces around a highly dominant garment.
Balance a visually heavy jacket with controlled lower-body details.
Avoid adding multiple competing focal elements.
rules.styling_tip: Ek piece dominant hai to baaki outfit ko comparatively controlled rakho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_transition_at_waist
rules.guideline: The transition between top and bottom should remain visually clean whether the outfit is tucked, untucked or layered.
recommendations: Avoid excessive fabric accumulation around the waistband.
Choose top length that supports the intended waist transition.
Keep visible waistband details intentional.
rules.styling_tip: Waist area mein unnecessary fabric bunching outfit ko messy dikha sakti hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_detail_competition
rules.guideline: Multiple highly detailed garments should not compete equally for attention.
recommendations: Pair a heavily detailed piece with cleaner supporting garments.
Avoid combining multiple statement graphics, hardware-heavy pieces and complex textures.
Let one major detail establish the visual character of the outfit.
rules.styling_tip: Agar jacket detailed hai, toh tee aur bottom comparatively clean rakhna better balance deta hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_anchor_distribution
rules.guideline: Distribute visually important garments across the outfit so one area does not feel unintentionally overloaded.
recommendations: Avoid concentrating all noticeable details around one small body area.
Use simpler surrounding garments when one zone already has strong visual information.
Check the outfit as a complete front-facing composition.
rules.styling_tip: Details ko ek hi jagah overload mat karo; outfit mein visual balance distribute karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_line_direction
rules.guideline: The directional lines created by garment seams, openings and edges should work together rather than create visual confusion.
recommendations: Use vertical garment lines to support a clean elongated appearance.
Avoid too many competing diagonal details in a minimal outfit.
Consider how jackets, shirts and trousers create continuous visual lines.
rules.styling_tip: Garments ki lines ek dusre ko visually support karein, fight nahi.

rules.name: outfit_garment_opening_balance
rules.guideline: Visible openings such as shirt fronts, jacket openings and neck areas should maintain a controlled visual balance.
recommendations: Avoid exposing multiple large openings simultaneously without styling intent.
Keep the neckline and front opening proportionate to the outfit.
Use closed layers when the outfit already has substantial visual exposure.
rules.styling_tip: Neck aur front openings ko controlled rakho, especially layered looks mein.

rules.name: outfit_garment_surface_transition
rules.guideline: Transitions between smooth, textured and structured garment surfaces should feel intentional.
recommendations: Use a smooth garment to visually calm a heavily textured piece.
Avoid combining several highly textured surfaces without a clear focal point.
Consider texture changes when garments overlap.
rules.styling_tip: Ek textured piece ke saath smoother fabrics outfit ko cleaner bana sakte hain.

rules.name: outfit_garment_proportion_breakpoint
rules.guideline: Intentional proportion changes should occur at visually meaningful points such as the waist, hip or knee.
recommendations: Use garment hems to create deliberate proportion breaks.
Avoid random hem positions that make the silhouette look accidental.
Check how top, bottom and footwear create successive visual sections.
rules.styling_tip: Hemline kaha end ho rahi hai, woh overall silhouette ko kaafi affect karta hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_proportion_repetition
rules.guideline: Repeated proportions across multiple garments can make an outfit look predictable, so vary proportions intentionally when needed.
recommendations: Avoid giving every garment the same visual length.
Use different but compatible proportions between layers.
Keep repeated proportions when a deliberately uniform look is intended.
rules.styling_tip: Har layer ko same length dene ke bajaye controlled variation try karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_alignment
rules.guideline: Important garment edges and construction lines should align naturally with the body's main visual structure.
recommendations: Check whether hems and openings sit naturally around the body.
Avoid styling that creates accidental-looking misalignment.
Use intentional asymmetry only when it contributes to the design.
rules.styling_tip: Hems aur openings body ke natural structure ke saath aligned feel hone chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_detail_spacing
rules.guideline: Small garment details should have enough visual spacing to remain individually readable.
recommendations: Avoid clustering several small details in the same area.
Allow clean space around buttons, graphics or hardware.
Use spacing to prevent subtle details from visually merging.
rules.styling_tip: Chhote details ko breathing space do, warna outfit unnecessarily busy lag sakta hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_transition_speed
rules.guideline: Visual changes between garment sections should occur at a controlled pace rather than changing dramatically at every layer.
recommendations: Keep neighbouring garments relatively compatible in visual character.
Avoid sudden shifts between extremely minimal and highly elaborate pieces.
Use one strong transition when the outfit needs visual energy.
rules.styling_tip: Har layer mein dramatic change mat lao; visual transition ko controlled rakho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_detail_repetition
rules.guideline: Repeated small design details can create cohesion when they appear deliberately across different parts of an outfit.
recommendations: Repeat a subtle design element through accessories or garment details.
Keep repeated elements limited so they do not become visually excessive.
Use repetition to connect otherwise different pieces.
rules.styling_tip: Ek subtle detail ko 2 jagah repeat karna outfit mein cohesion create kar sakta hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_context_switch
rules.guideline: The same garment can communicate different style directions depending on the pieces and accessories paired with it.
recommendations: Evaluate garments as part of the complete outfit rather than judging them in isolation.
Use footwear and accessories to shift the style direction of versatile basics.
Preserve the garment's core character while adapting the surrounding pieces.
rules.styling_tip: Same shirt casual bhi lag sakti hai aur smart bhi, pairing uska context change karti hai.

rules.name: outfit_style_language_consistency
rules.guideline: Individual garments should communicate a compatible style language unless intentional contrast is being created.
recommendations: Pair relaxed garments with accessories that support the relaxed character.
Avoid mixing strongly contrasting style languages without a clear transition piece.
Use one contrasting element when a deliberate fashion contrast is desired.
rules.styling_tip: Outfit ke pieces ki overall 'language' compatible honi chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_statement_piece_support
rules.guideline: A statement garment works more effectively when supporting pieces leave enough attention for it.
recommendations: Identify the strongest statement piece before adding accessories.
Keep supporting garments visually controlled.
Avoid adding another equally dominant piece unless intentional contrast is required.
rules.styling_tip: Statement piece choose karne ke baad baaki outfit ko usko support karne do.

rules.name: outfit_neutral_support_for_statement
rules.guideline: Neutral supporting garments can provide visual space around a strong colour, print or design element.
recommendations: Use neutral basics around bold statement pieces.
Reduce competing colours when the main garment already has strong visual impact.
Keep accessories restrained when the statement piece is highly noticeable.
rules.styling_tip: Bold piece ko highlight karna hai to neutral surroundings kaafi effective hote hain.

rules.name: outfit_style_contrast_bridge
rules.guideline: When combining two different style directions, an intermediate garment or accessory can make the transition feel intentional.
recommendations: Use an overshirt, sneaker or accessory as a bridge between contrasting styles.
Avoid abrupt transitions between highly formal and highly casual pieces.
Keep the bridge element visually compatible with both sides.
rules.styling_tip: Formal + casual mix karte waqt ek bridge piece transition ko natural bana sakta hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_fastening_consistency
rules.guideline: Visible garment fastenings should support the intended styling state instead of appearing accidentally unfinished.
recommendations: Keep buttoning or fastening consistent with the outfit's intended formality.
Avoid random combinations of closed and open fasteners.
Use partially fastened garments intentionally when creating a relaxed look.
rules.styling_tip: Buttons ya zippers kitne open hain, woh intentional styling decision lagna chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_fold_direction
rules.guideline: Natural fabric folds should support the garment's intended fit and movement rather than creating misleading visual signals.
recommendations: Do not interpret every fold as evidence of poor fit.
Check whether folds originate from movement, posture or garment construction.
Recommend fit changes only when repeated folds indicate a consistent issue.
rules.styling_tip: Ek single crease dekhkar fit judge mat karo; repeated fold pattern dekho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_visual_center
rules.guideline: The apparent visual center of an outfit should remain intentional when strong details are distributed across different garments.
recommendations: Check where the eye naturally lands first.
Avoid accidental visual concentration caused by unrelated details.
Use one dominant area when a clear outfit direction is intended.
rules.styling_tip: Outfit ko dekhte hi eye sabse pehle kahan ja rahi hai, usse visual center samjho.

rules.name: outfit_garment_state_consistency
rules.guideline: Garments should appear in styling states that make sense together, such as worn, rolled, tucked or layered.
recommendations: Keep similar styling decisions consistent across related garments.
Avoid mixing overly structured and extremely relaxed garment states without purpose.
Treat rolled sleeves, tucked hems and open layers as intentional choices.
rules.styling_tip: Tuck, roll aur open-layer jaise styling states ek dusre ke saath logically match hone chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_visual_interruption
rules.guideline: Unnecessary interruptions between major outfit elements can weaken the clarity of the overall look.
recommendations: Identify accessories or garment details that unnecessarily break the visual flow.
Keep transitions between major pieces readable.
Retain interruptions only when they contribute to the intended style.
rules.styling_tip: Jo detail outfit ke flow ko bina reason break kar rahi ho, use simplify karna better ho sakta hai.

rules.name: outfit_weather_layer_priority
rules.guideline: When weather requires layering, prioritize the layer that provides the needed function while keeping the visible styling coherent.
recommendations: Choose the functional outer layer first for cold or rain.
Build the visible outfit around that layer.
Avoid adding unnecessary layers only for visual complexity.
rules.styling_tip: Weather ke hisaab se functional layer pehle decide karo, phir styling build karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_usage_signal
rules.guideline: Garments should visually communicate their intended use when the outfit is built for a specific activity.
recommendations: Use practical pieces for active or movement-heavy settings.
Avoid styling delicate or restrictive garments for activities they do not support.
Let footwear and accessories reinforce the activity context.
rules.styling_tip: Gym, travel ya daily wear mein outfit ko activity ka signal bhi dena chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_layer_removability
rules.guideline: In outfits expected to move between temperature or indoor conditions, removable layers should remain visually complete when taken off.
recommendations: Ensure the base outfit works independently from the outer layer.
Avoid relying on an outer garment to hide unfinished styling.
Use removable layers that complement rather than define the entire outfit.
rules.styling_tip: Jacket utarne ke baad bhi base outfit complete aur intentional lagna chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_activity_transition
rules.guideline: An outfit should remain visually coherent when the wearer changes posture or activity within the same setting.
recommendations: Consider how the outfit looks while standing, walking and sitting.
Avoid styling elements that become impractical during normal movement.
Keep important visual details visible across common positions.
rules.styling_tip: Outfit sirf standing pose mein nahi, movement ke time bhi sensible hona chahiye.

rules.name: outfit_garment_recovery_after_movement
rules.guideline: Garments that return neatly to their intended shape after normal movement help maintain a consistently polished appearance.
recommendations: Prefer garments that do not permanently collapse after minor movement.
Consider stretch and fabric recovery for fitted or active pieces.
Avoid styling combinations that require constant manual adjustment.
rules.styling_tip: Aisa outfit better hota hai jo thodi movement ke baad bhi easily presentable rahe.

rules.name: outfit_garment_identity_separation
rules.guideline: When multiple garments have similar colours, textures or shapes, the AI should distinguish them before making styling recommendations.
recommendations: Identify each visible garment separately before evaluating the outfit.
Do not treat overlapping garments as a single clothing item.
Use visible construction details to distinguish similar pieces.
rules.styling_tip: Similar-looking layers ko pehle separately identify karo, phir styling judge karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_partial_visibility
rules.guideline: Partially visible garments should not be assigned highly specific attributes unless enough visual evidence is available.
recommendations: Use broad garment categories when only a small portion is visible.
Avoid guessing exact garment type from insufficient evidence.
Lower recommendation confidence when important clothing areas are hidden.
rules.styling_tip: Garment ka sirf thoda part dikh raha ho to exact type guess mat karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_attribute_uncertainty
rules.guideline: When an attribute such as fabric, fit or colour cannot be confidently identified from an image, the AI should avoid treating the assumption as fact.
recommendations: Separate observed attributes from inferred attributes.
Use cautious wording when image evidence is limited.
Base strong recommendations only on sufficiently visible characteristics.
rules.styling_tip: Jo image se clearly confirm nahi hai, usse fact ki tarah assume mat karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_occlusion_priority
rules.guideline: When an important garment is partially hidden, the AI should prioritize clearly visible elements over uncertain hidden details.
recommendations: Base the primary recommendation on unobstructed garments.
Treat hidden garment characteristics as uncertain.
Avoid changing the recommendation solely because of an unverified hidden detail.
rules.styling_tip: Jo clearly visible hai usko priority do; hidden details par unnecessary assumptions mat banao.

rules.name: outfit_garment_attribute_conflict
rules.guideline: If different visible cues suggest conflicting garment attributes, the AI should resolve the conflict before giving a specific recommendation.
recommendations: Compare colour, texture, construction and silhouette cues together.
Prefer multiple consistent visual signals over a single ambiguous cue.
If the conflict cannot be resolved, keep the recommendation general.
rules.styling_tip: Ek visual cue aur doosra cue conflict kare to pehle evidence compare karo, direct guess mat karo.

rules.name: outfit_worn_vs_carried_item
rules.guideline: The AI should distinguish between items being worn and items merely held or carried before evaluating the outfit.
recommendations: Do not count a jacket held in the hand as part of the worn outfit.
Do not treat a bag or accessory being carried as a worn accessory.
Evaluate only actively worn pieces when describing the current outfit.
rules.styling_tip: Jo item banda pehna nahi hai, usko outfit ka worn part mat count karo.

rules.name: outfit_reflection_vs_garment_detail
rules.guideline: The AI should distinguish reflections, highlights and environmental effects from actual garment colours or design details.
recommendations: Do not classify a bright reflection as a separate colour panel.
Check whether a visible highlight follows the garment surface.
Use the dominant underlying garment appearance for colour identification.
rules.styling_tip: Light reflection ko garment ka actual colour ya design detail mat samjho.

rules.name: outfit_background_vs_garment_boundary
rules.guideline: The AI should distinguish garment edges from visually similar background elements before identifying garment shape.
recommendations: Check whether an apparent garment extension follows the body.
Do not interpret background objects as part of clothing.
Use multiple visible edges to determine the actual garment boundary.
rules.styling_tip: Background aur garment same tone ke ho to boundary carefully identify karo.

rules.name: outfit_accessory_attachment_check
rules.guideline: Accessories should be identified based on how they are attached or positioned on the wearer rather than from shape alone.
recommendations: Distinguish worn accessories from nearby objects.
Check whether an item is actually attached to the body or garment.
Avoid identifying random visible objects as accessories.
rules.styling_tip: Accessory identify karte waqt uski placement aur attachment bhi check karo.

rules.name: outfit_garment_front_back_identification
rules.guideline: The AI should determine whether a visible garment section belongs to the front or back before interpreting its styling details.
recommendations: Use neckline, buttons, pockets and seams as orientation clues.
Do not apply front-specific styling advice to a back-facing garment.
When orientation is unclear, keep the garment analysis general.
rules.styling_tip: Front aur back orientation confirm karke hi garment details par recommendation do.

rules.name: outfit_intended_vs_accidental_styling
rules.guideline: The AI should distinguish deliberate styling choices from temporary or accidental garment positions before recommending changes.
recommendations: Do not automatically treat a slightly open shirt or rolled sleeve as a styling mistake.
Consider whether the garment position appears intentional and consistent.
Recommend changes only when the current styling clearly conflicts with the outfit goal.
rules.styling_tip: Har unusual styling ko mistake mat samjho; intentional styling bhi ho sakti hai.

rules.name: outfit_garment_wear_state
rules.guideline: The AI should account for whether a garment is being actively worn, temporarily adjusted or loosely positioned before evaluating its appearance.
recommendations: Distinguish normal wear from temporary adjustment.
Do not recommend permanent garment changes based on a temporary position.
Consider repeated visual evidence before identifying a wear-state issue.
rules.styling_tip: Temporary adjustment ko permanent fit problem samajhkar recommendation mat do.

rules.name: outfit_image_crop_context
rules.guideline: Recommendations should account for which parts of the outfit are actually visible within the image crop.
recommendations: Avoid judging footwear when the feet are outside the frame.
Avoid making full-outfit proportion claims from a partial crop.
